result.summary: Verdict as of 2026-10-14: run the 24/7 sales agent on an Anthropic API key (Console workspace, Commercial Terms), not on a Pro/Max subscription login. The Consumer Terms bar automated or bot access except via an API key, and the Claude Code legal page says developers building products should use API keys. Suggested split: (a) 24/7 WhatsApp inbox = Claude Agent SDK as a systemd service on the existing VPS behind the Flask webhook, with PreToolUse hooks and per-conversation budgets; (b) daily discovery and outreach = cron running claude -p --bare with hard limits, or a Managed Agents scheduled deployment; (c) long creative jobs (landing page, video) = a Managed Agents session (cloud sandbox, 0.08 USD per running hour plus tokens). Managed Agents is beta and is not Zero Data Retention or HIPAA eligible. Routines, Channels, /loop and GitHub Actions are not suitable as the always-on runtime. Biggest operational risk: a Console monthly spend cap (Start tier 500 USD) makes all API calls fail with HTTP 429 until the 1st of the next month, which would stop a 24/7 agent silently unless you monitor it.

findings.topic: Auth and billing: subscription login vs API key (quoted terms)
findings.detail: Consumer Terms Section 3 bans using the Services 'to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise', with the exception 'when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it'. Claude Code legal page: OAuth 'is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications'; developers building products or services 'should use API key authentication through Claude Console or a supported cloud provider'; Anthropic 'does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users'; Pro/Max limits 'assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK'. Agent SDK overview note: 'Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK.' Commercial Terms (effective June 17, 2025 per the fetched page) cover powering 'products and services Customer makes available to its own customers and end users', and restrict building competing products and reselling. Interpretation: a 24/7 agent messaging your leads is business automation and needs an API key. The legal page says to contact sales for edge cases.

findings.topic: Claude Code subscription token for CI and scripts
findings.detail: claude setup-token generates a one-year CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for a Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors), and bare mode does not read it. Auth precedence: cloud provider vars, then ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then apiKeyHelper, then CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, then profiles, then /login. In -p mode ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is always used when set, so a stray key silently switches billing to the API. For shared CI secrets, the GitHub Actions doc recommends an API key because an OAuth token is tied to the subscriber who generated it.

findings.topic: Claude Code headless mode (-p) for unattended runs
findings.detail: claude -p 'prompt' runs non-interactively. --output-format json returns result, session_id and total_cost_usd; stream-json streams events. --json-schema returns validated output in structured_output. --max-turns (no limit by default) exits with an error when reached. --max-budget-usd stops at an estimated spend (client-side, can overshoot, subagent spend counts). --permission-mode dontAsk denies anything not pre-approved; auto uses a classifier; acceptEdits auto-accepts edits. --allowedTools takes permission-rule syntax such as Bash(git diff *). --permission-prompts none (v2.1.259+) denies prompts with no one to answer them. --bare skips hooks, skills, MCP, CLAUDE.md and auto memory, is the recommended mode for scripts, and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (it never reads OAuth or keychain). Without --bare, -p runs project .claude/settings.json hooks and .mcp.json servers even in a folder you have never trusted. Exit code is non-zero on failure. SIGTERM exits 143 and leaves the turn unfinished. Background-work wait is capped at 10 minutes by default (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS). Sessions resume with --resume <id> or --continue; --no-session-persistence disables saving.

findings.topic: Hooks as hard guardrails (PreToolUse)
findings.detail: Events include SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, Stop, StopFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Notification, PreCompact and PostCompact. To block a PreToolUse call: exit code 2 (stderr is fed back to Claude; this overrides any allow JSON), or JSON hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName PreToolUse and permissionDecision of allow, deny, ask or defer plus permissionDecisionReason. Staying silent does not approve a call. updatedInput rewrites tool arguments before they run. Default timeout is 600 s for command, http and mcp_tool hooks; a timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block unless onFailure is set to block (v2.1.295+). A Stop hook can block stopping (exit 2 or decision block). The docs imply hooks run in -p mode but do not state it outright.

findings.topic: Claude Agent SDK (Python and TypeScript)
findings.detail: Packages: claude-agent-sdk (Python) and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (TypeScript). Built-in tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch. Limits: max_turns (tool round trips) and max_budget_usd (client-side estimate, can pass the value, leave headroom). ResultMessage.subtype can be success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd or error_during_execution. Check terminal_reason before subtype, because a failed final request can show success. In streaming mode total_cost_usd is cumulative, so read the last result rather than summing. ClaudeSDKClient keeps a multi-turn session open, with interrupt() and set_permission_mode(). query() is one-shot. Sessions: resume, session_id (UUID), fork_session. permission_mode values: default, acceptEdits, plan, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, auto. disallowed_tools supports scoped rules such as Bash(rm *). can_use_tool runs only when a call falls through to a prompt, and allowed_tools bypasses it. The docs say to use a PreToolUse hook to gate every call. Subagents are defined with the agents option. Custom tools and MCP servers plug in. Anthropic does not host Agent SDK apps; you host them.

findings.topic: Agent SDK hosting pattern and resources
findings.detail: Each agent session is one claude CLI subprocess that owns its shell, working directory and JSONL transcripts on local disk. Four session patterns are documented: ephemeral (one container per task), long-running (ClaudeSDKClient per session, in a container that exposes HTTP or WebSocket), hybrid (ephemeral containers hydrated from a SessionStore), and multi-agent container. Starting point per agent: 1 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, 1 CPU, sized by measured peak RSS. There is no top-level session timeout, so set max_turns. Local disk state is lost on restart unless you mirror transcripts with a SessionStore adapter. CLAUDE.md memory files are not covered by SessionStore. Route outbound traffic through an egress proxy with allowlists, and inject credentials there. Needs Python 3.10+ or Node 18+. Telemetry comes from OTEL_* env vars (prompt text and tool inputs excluded by default). Multi-tenant isolation: setting_sources=[], a per-tenant CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1.

findings.topic: Routines (Claude Code cloud automation, research preview)
findings.detail: A routine is a saved prompt plus repos plus connectors, run on Anthropic cloud (or your self-hosted environment). Triggers: schedule (minimum interval 1 hour; custom cron via /schedule update), API (POST to a per-routine /fire endpoint with a bearer token and optional text; beta header experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01; claude.ai users only, not part of the Platform API), and GitHub events (PR, release). Runs execute autonomously with no approval prompts, and all connectors you attach can write without asking. Limits: 100 scheduled runs per hour per account; 30 per hour per routine for Run now plus API fires (shared); 100 API fires per hour per account; GitHub events capped per routine and account; no overage on these caps. Routines draw down subscription usage. Available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. Routines belong to one person's claude.ai account, and Team/Enterprise owners can disable them. RemoteTrigger was not found in the docs I read; the closest documented thing is the /fire API.

findings.topic: Other Claude Code scheduling options (not 24/7 runtimes)
findings.detail: /loop and in-session cron run only while the session is open; tasks expire after 7 days; a session holds at most 50 tasks; they restore on --resume except expired ones. Desktop scheduled tasks run on your own machine. Channels (research preview) push Telegram, Discord or iMessage events, or custom webhooks, into a running session; they require claude.ai or Console API key auth, are not available on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, and events arrive only while the session is open. GitHub Actions: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 with a schedule cron trigger; scheduled runs use the default branch only; GitHub disables schedules in public repos after 60 days of inactivity; Actions minutes are billed; pass --max-turns in claude_args.

findings.topic: Managed Agents: what it is and availability
findings.detail: Beta, header managed-agents-2026-04-01 (the SDK sets it), enabled by default for all API accounts. Concepts: Agent (model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, skills; create once, reference by ID), Environment (Anthropic cloud sandbox or self-hosted), Session (running instance), Events (user.message, tool results, status; streamed over SSE; history stored server-side). Built-in tools: bash, file read/write/edit/glob/grep, web search and fetch (with domain allow or block lists), MCP servers. Sessions are stateful, resume after pauses, and store history and sandbox state server-side. Not eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA. Sessions can be deleted via the API. Custom tools run in your application, not Anthropic's sandbox.

findings.topic: Managed Agents scheduled deployments and webhooks
findings.detail: Scheduled deployments: POST /v1/deployments with a cron expression (POSIX, minute granularity) and an IANA timezone, plus an initial user.message event. Max 1,000 deployments per org. Execution jitter is up to 15% of the interval (min 5 s, max 9 min). DST: wall-clock times skipped on spring-forward do not fire; ambiguous times fire twice; avoid 1 to 3 AM. Pause suppresses future triggers but not running sessions; unpause does not backfill; archive is terminal. Failed runs are listed with error types such as session_rate_limited_error (not retried until next occurrence), and unrecoverable errors auto-pause the deployment. Webhooks are outbound notifications from Anthropic to you, not inbound triggers: to start work you call the Sessions API yourself. Event types include session.status_idled, session.status_run_started, session.budget_reached, session.status_terminated, deployment_run.failed and others. Endpoints must be HTTPS on port 443 with a public hostname; verify with ANTHROPIC_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY via SDK unwrap() (rejects payloads older than 5 minutes). Delivery: up to 3 attempts with 5 to 120 s jittered backoff; not a durable log; deduplicate on event id; reconcile by GET. Endpoints auto-disable on 3xx, non-public IP, or sustained failure.

findings.topic: Managed Agents session budgets
findings.detail: Create a session with budget {type: limit, max_list_cost: {amount: '<whole US cents as a string>', currency: 'USD'}}; a budget can only be added at creation (not later), but it can be raised, lowered or removed later. It is measured at public list rates (not your contracted price). Components: model tokens at each model's list price, web search at 10 USD per 1,000, and session running time at 0.08 USD per hour. Enforced between model requests, so spend can exceed the cap by about one request per thread. At the cap the session goes idle with stop_reason budget_reached (not terminated) and emits session.budget_reached. Accepted events at the cap are only tool confirmations, tool results and interrupts; user.message is rejected with 400. Resume by raising the cap above consumed list cost (400 if not above). A deployment's budget is copied onto each run separately, not cumulative across runs.

findings.topic: Managed Agents pricing (session runtime)
findings.detail: Billed on two dimensions: tokens at the Model pricing rates (with cache multipliers, and 1.1x if inference_geo is us, and fast-mode premium if used), plus session runtime at 0.08 USD per session-hour, metered only while status is running. Idle time (waiting for your message or a tool confirmation), rescheduling and terminated time are free. Batch discount does not apply to sessions. Worked example from the page: a 1-hour Opus 5.5 session with 50,000 input and 15,000 output tokens = 0.58 USD. Implication: a session that sleeps between WhatsApp messages costs only tokens. Running 24 hours a day costs 1.92 USD per day, roughly 58 USD per month, in runtime alone.

findings.topic: Managed Agents permission policies and approval gates
findings.detail: Policies: always_allow (runs with no confirmation), always_ask (session pauses until approval), and a server-evaluated mode where the server judges each call. MCP toolsets default to always_ask. To approve or deny, send user.tool_confirmation with tool_use_id (from stop_reason.event_ids of session.status_idle) and result allow or deny, plus an optional deny_message. Confirmations for calls the server already decided (not ask) are rejected with 400. IMPORTANT: custom tools run in your application and are NOT governed by permission policies, so a WhatsApp send tool or a publish tool must enforce its own approval gate in code.

findings.topic: Managed Agents multi-agent orchestration (beta)
findings.detail: Multiagent configuration type multiagent_20261001. Two mechanisms: subagents (the agent delegates and reads reports; up to 20 predefined agents) and dynamic workflows (the agent writes a program that runs many agents in the background; up to 20 predefined agents). Both are enabled by default for this type; workflows can be turned off with subagents disabled. An advisor model can be consulted. Agents run in parallel with isolated context. A multiagent session has one shared budget across all threads, with no per-thread caps. Advisor consultations count against the budget.

findings.topic: Managed Agents self-hosted sandboxes (beta)
findings.detail: Orchestration stays on Anthropic's side; tool execution runs on your own worker. The worker needs a Linux host with /bin/bash and outbound HTTPS only (it polls; no inbound port). Create a self-hosted environment, generate an environment key only in the Console, then run ant beta:worker poll --workdir /workspace. A session waits in the queue if no worker is connected. Tool inputs and outputs still flow through Anthropic's control plane. Self-hosted environments support memory_store resources only; file and github_repository resources are rejected. Whether runtime is billed for self-hosted sessions was not stated in the pages I read.

findings.topic: Current Claude models, IDs, context and per-MTok pricing
findings.detail: Current IDs (also the API aliases): claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5. All have a 1M-token context and 128K synchronous max output, and knowledge cutoff June 2026. Recommended default: Opus 5.5 for most workloads; Fable 5.1 for demanding long-horizon agentic work. Base input and output per MTok: Fable 5.1 10 and 50; Opus 5.5 4 and 20; Sonnet 5.5 2 and 10; Haiku 5.5 0.10 and 0.50 for prompts up to 100k tokens, rising to 0.50 and 2.50 above 100k (Haiku is the only model with a long-context price step). Batch input and output per MTok: Fable 5.1 5 and 25; Opus 5.5 2 and 10; Sonnet 5.5 1 and 5; Haiku 5.5 0.05 and 0.25 (up to 100k). Cache writes 5m and 1h per MTok: Fable 12.50 and 20; Opus 5 and 8; Sonnet 2.50 and 4; Haiku 0.125 and 0.20. Cache reads per MTok: Fable 0.25; Opus 0.20; Sonnet 0.10; Haiku 0.01. Data residency inference_geo us adds 1.1x. Web search is 10 USD per 1,000 searches. Fast mode is a research-preview premium on Opus models.

findings.topic: Cost example per WhatsApp turn (illustrative, my arithmetic on list prices)
findings.detail: Assumes 20k input tokens of which 16k are cache reads and 4k uncached, plus 1k output, and excludes cache writes. Sonnet 5.5: 4,000 x 2 + 16,000 x 0.10 + 1,000 x 10, per million, = about 0.0196 USD (about 2 cents per turn), so about 20 USD per 1,000 turns. Haiku 5.5 with the same shape = about 0.0011 USD per turn. Opus 5.5 with the same shape = about 0.042 USD per turn (4,000 x 4 + 16,000 x 0.20 + 1,000 x 20, per million).

findings.topic: Prompt caching rules
findings.detail: Minimum cacheable prompt length: 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1; shorter prompts are processed without caching and no error is returned. Default TTL is 5 minutes, refreshed at no cost on each use. 1-hour TTL via cache_control with ttl '1h', priced at 2x base input for writes versus 1.25x for 5-minute writes. Up to 4 cache breakpoints per request. Prefix order is tools, then system, then messages; a change at one level invalidates that level and everything after it. Cache reads cost 0.1x base (0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1). Keep the system prompt and tool definitions stable.

findings.topic: Batch API (Message Batches)
findings.detail: 50% discount on input and output. Up to 100,000 requests per batch on Start, Build and Scale tiers. Processing queue cap: 200k (Start), 300k (Build), 500k (Scale) requests. Most batches finish in under 1 hour. Results can be read when all requests finish or after 24 hours, whichever comes first. Unprocessed requests expire at 24 hours and are not billed. Results are downloadable for 29 days. Each request needs max_tokens of at least 1. Not for real-time work. Sessions in Managed Agents cannot use batches. I did not verify whether batches support tool-use loops, so do not assume they do.

findings.topic: Rate limits and spend caps (critical for 24/7)
findings.detail: Tiers Start, Build, Scale; new orgs may start on a lower Evaluation tier. Monthly spend caps: Start 500 USD, Build 1,000 USD, Scale 200,000 USD. When the cap is reached, all API requests return HTTP 429 with error.details.error_code enforced_spend_limit_reached, no retry-after header, and access returns at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the next month. You can also set your own lower workspace or org limit, which returns HTTP 400 invalid_request_error. Per-model RPM, ITPM, OTPM at Start: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 each 1,000 / 2,000,000 / 400,000; Fable 5.1 1,000 / 500,000 / 100,000 (shared with Fable 5). Build: 5,000 / 5,000,000 / 1,000,000 for the 5.5 models. Scale: 10,000 / 10,000,000 / 2,000,000. Cache reads do not count toward ITPM for these models. Managed Agents endpoints: 300 create requests per minute and 1,200 read requests per minute per org. Tier qualification thresholds were not fetched.

findings.topic: Acceptable Use Policy items that matter for outreach
findings.detail: The AUP page I fetched shows 'Usage Policy (Effective November 12, 2026)'. Relevant items: bans promoting or facilitating 'the generation or distribution of spam' and automation 'to engage in spammy behavior'; consumer-facing chatbots or agents 'must disclose to users that they are interacting with AI rather than a human'; bans bots 'that claim to be human' and fake personas; bans misrepresenting or concealing sponsorship of messaging; bans compiling or enriching 'personal data from multiple sources to build profiles of individuals' for sale or disclosure without the individuals' awareness and agreement, and building dossiers on individuals. Enrichment at company level is the safer pattern. The page does not explicitly cover scraping personal information. I could not confirm which version is in force today.

findings.topic: Observability and kill switches
findings.detail: Managed Agents: session event stream includes session.usage snapshots (tokens, list_cost, active_seconds); webhooks for state changes; deployment runs list with has_error=true; pause a deployment with POST /v1/deployments/{id}/pause (running sessions continue; manual run still allowed); send user.interrupt to stop a turn; lowering or removing a session budget pauses work. Agent SDK: total_cost_usd and model_usage (client-side estimates, not billing), api_retry events, OTel export, interrupt(). Claude Code -p: --output-format json reports total_cost_usd; --include-hook-events exposes hook activity; SIGINT ends the current turn; SIGTERM exits 143; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 disables the scheduler.

recommendations: Billing: create a dedicated Anthropic Console workspace and API key for the agent (Developer role for the owner or engineer who holds it). Set a workspace spend limit below your tier cap and alert on it. Store the key only in a 0600 env file on the VPS, never in chat or in the repo. Do not run the 24/7 agent on a Pro/Max login or a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

Role (a), 24/7 webhook inbox: use the Claude Agent SDK (Python 3.10+) as a systemd service on the existing VPS. Flask receives the WhatsApp webhook and writes each event to a queue table in SQLite (WAL) or Postgres, so nothing is lost on restart. A worker processes one lead conversation at a time with ClaudeSDKClient, keyed by lead ID, with SessionStore on the same DB. Set max_turns around 15 to 20 and max_budget_usd per turn with headroom. Route models: Haiku 5.5 for triage, Sonnet 5.5 for replies, Opus 5.5 for pitch planning, Fable 5.1 only on escalation.

Role (a) guardrails: add a PreToolUse hook that denies the send tool unless the lead has opted in, the message is an approved template or inside the allowed window, and the daily per-lead and global caps are not exceeded. Deny every tool not on an explicit allowlist. Make CRM writes in-process tools that call your own Flask or DB functions, never raw SQL. Have the agent identify itself as AI in the first message.

Role (a) alternative: Managed Agents session per lead (POST /v1/sessions with a budget, one user.message per inbound message, subscribe to session.status_idled and session.budget_reached webhooks). Choose this only if you accept beta status and that data is not ZDR or HIPAA eligible. Gate the send tool in your own code, because custom tools are not covered by permission policies.

Role (b), daily discovery and outreach: start with a VPS cron job running claude -p --bare --output-format json --max-turns N --max-budget-usd X --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools with an explicit list, plus --permission-prompts none. Check subtype, is_error and permission_denials in the JSON, and log total_cost_usd. For bulk single-shot pitch or copy drafts, use the Batch API (50% off, up to 100k requests per batch, results within about 24 h). Graduate to a Managed Agents scheduled deployment if you want Anthropic to run the cron and keep run history.

Role (c), long creative tasks (landing page plus video): use a Managed Agents session, which has a cloud sandbox with bash, files and web, at 0.08 USD per running hour plus tokens, with a per-session budget. Wrap ElevenLabs and kie.ai as custom tools. Make the publish-to-ivinfotech.com step a custom tool that writes to a staging area and waits for a human approval flag in your DB, because custom tools bypass permission policies. The VPS-based Agent SDK with a per-job working directory is the alternative if you want all data on your server.

Multi-agent design (my recommendation, not a documented best practice): run four roles (Discovery, Enrich and Pitch, Creative and Outreach, Inbox) as separate processes or sessions, each with its own tool allowlist and budget. Coordinate through CRM state rows in the DB rather than agent-to-agent chat. Use separate keys or workspaces per role so spend is visible per role.

Minimal server setup on the existing VPS: Python 3.10+ (or Node 18+ for the TypeScript SDK); systemd units with Restart=always and EnvironmentFile at 0600; SQLite WAL or Postgres for the queue and SessionStore; a /healthz endpoint; JSON-lines logs per turn (subtype, cost, tokens) and per tool call; a kill-switch flag row in the DB that the PreToolUse hook and the worker check before every turn; daily spend reconciliation against the Console usage page. Budget about 1 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk and 1 CPU per concurrent agent subprocess, sized from measured peak RSS.

Cost control: keep system prompts and tool definitions stable and above 512 tokens so they cache, and use the 1-hour cache TTL only for conversations that pause for more than 5 minutes. Route classification to Haiku 5.5, replies to Sonnet 5.5, and escalation to Opus 5.5.

Outreach compliance (from the AUP and Consumer Terms): disclose AI identity to leads, use no fake personas, disclose sponsorship, honor opt-outs immediately, enrich at company level rather than building personal profiles, and keep personal data in your own DB rather than in prompts beyond what each turn needs. Meta WhatsApp policy (template approval, messaging window, AI-initiated messages) is a separate requirement that I did not research; check Meta's policy before going live.
risks: Subscription misuse: running a 24/7 business agent on a Pro/Max login conflicts with Consumer Terms Section 3 and the Claude Code legal page. The legal page says Anthropic reserves the right to enforce these restrictions without prior notice.

Spend-cap outage: on the Start tier (500 USD monthly cap), reaching the cap returns HTTP 429 enforced_spend_limit_reached on every request, with no retry-after, until the 1st of the next month. SDK auto-retries will also fail. A 24/7 agent can go dark mid-month without warning unless you alert on spend.

Managed Agents is beta (header managed-agents-2026-04-01), so behavior may change. Conversation history and sandbox state are stored server-side, and it is not ZDR or HIPAA eligible, which matters for lead personal data.

Custom tools are not governed by permission policies. A prompt-injected inbound WhatsApp message could make the agent call a send or publish tool. Enforce approval gates in your own code or hooks, and do not put secrets in the agent environment.

Budgets are estimates or list-price: SDK max_budget_usd is a client-side estimate that can overshoot. Managed Agents budgets are list-price, enforced between requests, and can overshoot by about one request per thread. Neither equals your invoice.
Managed webhooks are not durable: each event gets 3 attempts with 5 to 120 s backoff, then it is dropped with no signal. Reconcile by GET, and deduplicate on event id.

Routines and Channels are research preview. Routines run with no approval prompts and include all attached connectors by default, including write tools, so do not put outbound sales messages into a routine. Channels need an open terminal session.

Without --bare, claude -p runs the project's .claude/settings.json hooks and .mcp.json servers even in untrusted folders. Use --bare on servers. Note that --bare requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, since it never reads OAuth or keychain credentials.
Setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment makes -p runs use the API key even when a subscription login exists. Set it deliberately on the server only.
Kill mid-turn: SIGTERM exits 143 and leaves the turn unfinished. Resume behavior needs CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1 if you want the turn finished on resume.
Prompt injection through inbound lead messages is the main abuse path for an inbox agent. Treat all inbound text as untrusted data, and keep the agent unable to act outside the allowlist.

result.summary:
VERDICT: Meta's policy text has no B2B or published-number exemption. A marketing template to a business owner whose number you scraped from their website, Facebook page or ad is not valid opt-in as written. Enforcement is reactive (blocks, reports, negative feedback), which is why vendors say it "works" until it doesn't. The risk ladder is: warning, then 1-3 day template block, then 5/7/30-day full send block, then account lock, then permanent disablement. So WhatsApp should NOT be the cold first touch to scraped numbers. It should be the conversation channel after the lead raises a hand (taps a wa.me link, replies, or clicks a Click-to-WhatsApp ad) or opts in.

KEY FACTS (as of 2026-10-14):
- New Meta business portfolios are capped at 250 unique recipients per rolling 24h outside customer-service windows. The cap is portfolio-level and shared by all numbers. Business verification lifts it to 2,000, and higher tiers are automatic after that.
- India rates (ex-18% GST): marketing about Rs 0.8631, utility/authentication Rs 0.115, per delivered message.
- The 2026-10-01 change: in-window service (free-form) messages are now billable. Each number gets 1,000 free per month, then about Rs 0.115. Meta's own FAQ confirms this. Utility templates inside an open window also became billable (vendor-reported, plus a GitHub issue quoting Meta's updated page). Marketing pricing is unchanged.
- I could not find the VRP Tech LinkedIn post. The Oct-1 change above is almost certainly what it refers to.
- For India-billed WABAs, INR migration is due by 2026-12-31, or delivery stops on 2027-01-01. Check this with the BSP now.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE (full version in recommendations): (1) first touch by email, contact form or LinkedIn carrying the personalised landing page and video link plus a wa.me deep link to your verified number; (2) when the lead messages in, a 24h window opens, so the agent replies free-form with the pitch, video and landing page and captures explicit named opt-in, logged in the CRM; (3) only opted-in leads get follow-up marketing templates with a Stop quick-reply button, capped at about 1/week and 3 touches; (4) optionally add Click-to-WhatsApp ads and Custom Audiences, which are practical but need rights to the list and have low B2B match rates; (5) keep strict limits and auto-pause on any quality signal.

findings.topic: 1a. Opt-in: what Meta's text actually requires
findings.detail: The WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy says businesses may contact people only if the person has given them their mobile number or username AND the business has received opt-in permission from the recipient confirming they wish to receive subsequent messages. Opt-in must clearly state that the person is opting in to receive communication from the business and must name the business. The business chooses the method (SMS, website, IVR phone flow, in person/paper), and the opt-in can be general, not WhatsApp-specific, if it follows local law. Meta recommends separate opt-in by message category. The policy also says: do not 'confuse, deceive, defraud, mislead, spam, or surprise' people. Outside the 24h window you may only message with approved templates. The Meta opt-in page does not address B2B, published business numbers, or whether a Click-to-WhatsApp ad click counts as opt-in. The policy has no explicit rule on purchased or scraped lists.

findings.topic: 1b. Is a marketing template to a business owner whose number is published online allowed?
findings.detail: As written, no. A number published on a site/FB page/ad is neither 'given to you' nor an opt-in 'to receive messages from a particular business' that names you. Meta has no B2B or public-listing carve-out. This is my reading of the text, supported by consistent vendor guidance that scraped, purchased or publicly listed numbers are not valid opt-in. Practical reality: Meta says it uses automated and human review and 'may reactively review opt-in flows'. In practice, enforcement is triggered by recipient blocks/reports and negative feedback, not by checking provenance. So it is a policy violation with probabilistic enforcement, not a technical block. The only clearly compliant ways to message a cold lead are a user-initiated chat (wa.me link, reply, ad click) or an opt-in captured elsewhere (website form, SMS, email reply, in person). Opt-in can also be requested inside a WhatsApp thread the user started. That last point is from vendor docs, not Meta's opt-in page.

findings.topic: 1c. Consequences (enforcement ladder)
findings.detail: Meta policy: WhatsApp 'may limit or remove your access' on 'significant amounts of negative feedback' or violations. User feedback can trigger automated sending limits. Terminated accounts may be barred from all future use of WhatsApp products. Enforcement doc escalation: (1) warning naming the policy; (2) 1- or 3-day block on marketing/utility/authentication templates and on adding phone numbers; (3) 5-, 7- or 30-day block on sending any message; (4) account lock until appeal; (5) permanent disablement from the Platform. Appeals go through Business Support Home (24-48h typical), and 'not all spam violations might be appealed'. Related signals: error 131048 means the sender number is restricted, likely from blocked/spam-flagged messages. Error 131049 means the message was withheld to protect 'healthy ecosystem engagement' (per-user marketing cap). Template quality is GREEN/YELLOW/RED, driven by negative feedback and read rates. Template pausing goes 3h, then 6h, then disabled on the 3rd instance. Paused sends are not billed. Template misclassification (utility submitted that is really marketing) has its own ladder: warning, then utility rate-limit for at least 7 days, then 7/30-day utility-template restriction, then a 30-day business-portfolio-level restriction. Note that the portfolio is the enforcement unit for that last step.

findings.topic: 2a. Template categories and the cold-intro trap
findings.detail: Three categories: marketing, utility, authentication. Marketing covers awareness, sales, retargeting and relationship-building. Mixed content (e.g. an order update with a promo) is marketing. Unclear content (a lone variable or a generic greeting) is marketing. Utility must be non-promotional AND tied to a user request or essential. 'Moving a conversation to WhatsApp' is utility only if the user requested it. So a cold intro must be submitted as MARKETING. Do not disguise it as utility: Meta auto-recategorises utility to marketing, and for businesses with a misuse warning the change is instant with no notice. Repeat misuse triggers the restriction ladder in 1c. Authentication is OTP-only, with no URLs, media or emoji. Misclassified templates can be appealed within 60 days.

findings.topic: 2b. Approval process and rejection reasons
findings.detail: Templates are reviewed automatically on creation/edit. A decision can take up to 24h (Meta). Vendors report most are decided in minutes (unverified). Statuses: In Review, Approved (Active - Quality pending), Rejected, Paused, Disabled. A rejected template can be edited and resubmitted, or appealed (an appeal must include a sample). Appeals are decided within 24h. Rejection reasons per Meta: (a) a variable at the start or end ('cannot start or end with a parameter'); (b) bad parameter format (mismatched braces, special characters like #$%, non-sequential numbering, too many variables for the text length); (c) policy violations (Commerce/Business Policy, sensitive identifiers, abusive language); (d) emoji/character limits; (e) duplicate body+footer of an existing template; (f) wrong category. Vendor-reported extras (not Meta text): avoid URL shorteners and wa.me links inside the template body, and avoid excess consecutive spaces/newlines. Limits: 250 templates per WABA if unverified, up to 6,000 if verified with an approved display name; 100 template creations per hour. Sample values are required for every variable.

findings.topic: 2c. Header video/image and button rules
findings.detail: Media headers (image, video, GIF [Marketing Messages API only], document) require an asset handle from the Resumable Upload API at creation. The sample media is reviewed. Cloud API media limits: video MP4 or 3GPP, H.264 video + AAC audio only, single audio stream, max 16 MB. Image JPEG/PNG, 8-bit RGB/RGBA, max 5 MB. Document max 100 MB. Text header max 60 chars with 1 variable. Body max 1,024 chars. Footer max 60 chars. Buttons: max 10 total; quick reply up to 10; URL buttons up to 2 (URL max 2,000 chars, one variable only at the very end); phone up to 1; copy-code up to 1; label max 25 chars. Quick-reply and non-quick-reply buttons must be in two contiguous groups. 4+ buttons, or quick reply mixed with other types, don't render on WhatsApp desktop. Meta suggests a quick reply such as 'Unsubscribe from Promos' for marketing opt-out, but does not mandate it. At send time, upload media and send its id (Meta recommends this); a 'link' must be publicly reachable or the send fails.

findings.topic: 3a. India pricing (per delivered message, ex-GST)
findings.detail: Per-message pricing has applied since 2025-07-01. India marketing rate was raised effective 2026-01-01. Secondary sources (Free Press Journal, citing Meta's rate card, and ChatMaxima, citing Meta's INR card) give marketing Rs 0.8631 (previously Rs 0.7846), utility Rs 0.115, authentication Rs 0.115, authentication-international Rs 2.4971. 18% GST is added (marketing becomes about Rs 1.02). Utility/authentication have volume tiers (up to -30%); marketing and service are not tiered. BSPs add markup (AiSensy lists Rs 1.09 marketing and Rs 0.145 utility). Meta's own page confirms 'India - higher marketing rate' on 2026-01-01 but I could not read the INR figures directly. Only delivered templates are charged. Rate changes only take effect on the first day of a quarter, with 1 month's notice for rate cards. India billing localisation: eligible WABAs must migrate to INR by 2026-12-31, or Meta stops delivering their messages from 2027-01-01. Rough planning cost: 1,000 delivered cold marketing templates is about Rs 1,018 with GST at Meta rates, before BSP markup. This is my arithmetic.

findings.topic: 3b. What changed on 2026-10-01 (VRP Tech post)
findings.detail: I could not find the VRP Tech LinkedIn post. The 2026-10-01 change that matches your description is: (1) free-form service messages sent inside the 24h customer-service window, free since 2024-11-01, are now billable per message. Each business phone number gets 1,000 free per calendar month (no rollover), billed from the 1,001st at the utility rate (India about Rs 0.115). This is confirmed on Meta's own FAQ ('Effective October 1, 2026... the first 1,000 service messages are free each month... Meta will charge as of the 1,001st') and in the Free Press Journal report citing Meta's rate card. (2) Utility templates sent inside an open window, free since 2025-07-01, are now charged from the first message with no free allowance. This is reported by Wati, respond.io, AiSensy and ChatMaxima, and by a GitHub issue quoting Meta's page updated 2026-09-30. I could NOT confirm it in my own fetch of Meta's pricing page, because the developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing copy is stale. It still says service is free and utility-in-window is free, and the GitHub issue documents that stale-copy problem. (3) Marketing, authentication, inbound messages and FEP windows are unchanged. Billing starts at 00:00 on 2026-10-01 in each WABA's timezone. Other Oct-1 rate-card changes are for Bangladesh, Iraq, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Morocco, Oman and Ukraine, not India. One vendor reports that accounts with no payment method won't have service messages delivered past the free 1,000, so keep the BSP wallet funded. This is vendor-reported and conflicting, so verify with the BSP. The AI-provider pricing policy (2026-02-16) exempts AI providers from the service-message update. That is irrelevant to your own agent.

findings.topic: 4a. 24-hour customer-service window
findings.detail: The window opens when a user messages you and is refreshed by each new inbound message. Inside it you can send non-template messages (text, media, interactive reply buttons/lists, etc.). These are now billable above 1,000 per number per month (see 3b). Outside it you can send only approved templates; a free-form attempt fails with error 131047. A marketing message sent while a window is open, after the user replied to a marketing template, does not count toward the per-user marketing cap. A user reply to your template therefore lets the agent send the full pitch, video and landing page link free-form. This is the economic and compliance sweet spot. Inbound messages are free.

findings.topic: 4b. Messaging limits and tiers
findings.detail: Limits cap unique WhatsApp numbers you can deliver to outside customer-service windows in a rolling 24h. Since 2025-10-07 they are set per business portfolio, shared by all numbers in it. New portfolios start at 250. Tiers: 250, then 2,000, 10,000, 100,000, then unlimited. Paths to 2,000: verify the business, have a partner verify it, or deliver 2,000 messages to unique numbers outside windows within 30 days using high-quality templates. After that, automatic scaling needs high-quality messages across all numbers/templates AND use of at least half the current limit in the last 7 days. The increase takes effect within 6h. The 'Flagged' state was removed, so a quality drop no longer lowers the limit. The consequences of poor quality are instead pausing, restrictions and offboarding. Per-user marketing caps are separate: WhatsApp limits how many marketing templates one user receives, based on that user's recent marketing read rate. Retry only after 24h; failure shows as 131049. Per-user limits are not active for EEA/UK/Japan/South Korea. Users can set 'Offers and announcements' to stop marketing; this appears as error 131050, don't retry, and the user_preferences webhook fires on stop/resume.

findings.topic: 5. Inbound webhook payloads and statuses
findings.detail: All arrive under entry[].changes[].value with field='messages'. Common: metadata.phone_number_id, contacts[].wa_id and profile.name. Each messages[] item has from, id (wamid), timestamp, type. Types: (a) text: text.body. (b) Template quick-reply tap: type='button', button.payload and button.text (both the label, e.g. 'Unsubscribe' unless you set a custom payload), plus context.id (the wamid of the template message tapped) and context.from. (c) type='interactive': interactive.type='button_reply' with button_reply.id and title, or 'list_reply' with list_reply.id, title and description. (d) image/audio/etc. (voice notes will be common in India), plus unsupported (errors[] on the message). statuses[]: sent, delivered, read, played, failed. Fields: id, status, timestamp, recipient_id, optional biz_opaque_callback_data (use it to tie to CRM lead ids), pricing{type: regular/free_customer_service/free_entry_point, category, pricing_model PMP}. Failed statuses carry errors[] {code,title,message,error_data.details}. A delivered+read at once skips the delivered webhook. Click-to-WhatsApp inbound messages carry a referral object: source_url, source_id, source_type, headline, body, media fields and ctwa_clid. Useful error codes: 131026 (undeliverable/not on WhatsApp), 131047 (outside window), 131048 (sender restricted), 131049 (ecosystem cap), 131050 (user stopped marketing), 131056 (pair rate limit), 130429 (throughput), 132000-132016 (template errors, 132015 paused, 132016 disabled). Other subscribable webhook fields are message_template_status_update, template_category_update, account_update, account_alerts and user_preferences; the first three were cited in the Meta docs I read.

findings.topic: 6a. Click-to-WhatsApp (CTWA) ads and opt-in
findings.detail: A user who taps a CTWA ad and messages you has initiated the conversation. This opens a 24h service window and, if you reply within 24h, a Free Entry Point (FEP) window in which all messages including templates are free. Meta's official pages I could read say 72h. Wati and respond.io report that ad-originated windows became up to 7 days from 2026-09-28 (Page CTA buttons stay at 72h). Treat 72h as the safe planning number. Meta's opt-in documentation is silent on whether an ad click equals marketing opt-in. WhatsApp's own ad guide says the consumer should opt in to WhatsApp messaging 'within 72 hours', and that the opt-in request should name the business and say what messages to expect. So capture explicit opt-in in the first thread rather than assuming the click is consent. The ad can attach a Welcome Message Sequence (text, prefilled message, ice-breaker quick replies), and the webhook gives ctwa_clid and ad source for CRM attribution.

findings.topic: 6b. Custom Audiences (upload phone/email of businesses, show a CTWA ad)
findings.detail: Allowed in principle, subject to Meta's Customer List Custom Audience Terms. I read these in Gujarati and am paraphrasing. They require that you have all necessary rights and permissions and a lawful basis to disclose and use the data, and that you comply with applicable law. Opted-out people must be removed, you can't sell or transfer audiences, and health/financial/children's data is excluded. The terms don't explicitly mention purchased lists. Scraped or purchased lists are therefore a compliance grey zone under the 'rights/lawful basis' clause, the same weakness as the WhatsApp opt-in problem. Practicality in India (vendor-level evidence only, no India-specific benchmark found): typical customer-list match rates are about 30-60%, and B2B lists built on corporate emails match as low as about 10-15%, because Meta matches personal identifiers. Phone numbers must include the country code (+91). Uploading several identifiers per person helps. You can't target one specific lead reliably. The ad creative can be segment-personalised (industry/city), not lead-personalised. Best fit: lookalike or interest/location targeting of Gujarat SMEs, plus Custom Audiences built only from lists you hold rights to (e.g. your own CRM, inbound leads, past customers, event sign-ups). The ad click then creates the compliant user-initiated chat. I did not verify Meta's minimum audience size.

findings.topic: 7a. BSP, verification, display name
findings.detail: Solution Partners (BSPs) can extend credit lines and invoice clients directly. Tech Providers cannot, and clients add their own payment method. Only Select/Premier Solution Partners can submit partner-led business verification on a client's behalf (average about 5 min, up to a few hours, 3 submissions per client). Verification is one path to the 2,000 limit. Without it the portfolio sits at 250 and the WABA at 250 templates. The display name is auto-reviewed when a higher messaging limit is reached; a change can be made 10 times per 30 days, and after approval you must re-register the number within 14 days. Vendor guidance for India: any of Certificate of Incorporation, GST, Udyam, Shop & Establishment licence, business PAN or IEC works; GST is not mandatory; the legal name must match Business Manager exactly; processing time varies (vendor estimates 1-7 business days). Quality rating is tracked per phone number, but the limit is per portfolio and the enforcement 'business portfolio-level restriction' exists. So one bad outbound number can endanger every number in the same portfolio. WhatsApp Business app coexistence (app + API on one number) exists, with caps such as 20 msg/s throughput and one number per coexistence WABA (vendor-reported). It is not a loophole for cold bulk.

findings.topic: 7b. Using an AI agent on WhatsApp
findings.detail: Meta Terms for the WhatsApp Business Platform (last modified 2026-09-23) section 4.7 bars AI/ML providers from using the Platform to make their AI the primary offering (aimed at ChatGPT-style general assistants, effective 2026-01-15). Press and Meta's statement to TechCrunch say businesses using AI for their own customer service are unaffected. An Ivinfotech sales agent replying about Ivinfotech's own services is a business use case, but the 'primary vs incidental' test is at Meta's discretion, so keep the agent task-focused (no open-ended 'ask me anything'). The same section prohibits letting WhatsApp Business Platform Data, including derived forms, be used to train or improve AI models. You may fine-tune a model for your exclusive use if the data doesn't spread to other models. Do not feed chat logs into any shared/third-party training pipeline. I found no Meta requirement to disclose that a bot is an AI (not verified).

findings.topic: 8. India-specific law layered on top
findings.detail: DPDP Rules were notified 2025-11-13. Immediate: Board and definitions. 2026-11-13: consent-manager registration. 2027-05-13: the substantive duties (notice and consent, safeguards, breach notice, data-principal rights). The text I read does not address B2B contact data; sole proprietors' and owners' phone numbers are personal data, so plan to hold consent/notice records before May 2027. This is my inference. TRAI's TCCCPR/DLT regime governs SMS and calls, not WhatsApp. Airtel and the telcos have lobbied to extend it to OTT apps, and a draft TRAI Third Amendment (2026) is reported (29 April 2026) to touch third-party apps. IAMAI says OTT is out of TRAI's remit. It is a draft with no confirmed effective date, so no current legal obligation, but the direction is toward more regulation. If you use SMS as a channel, DLT-registered headers/templates are mandatory. Instagram/Messenger DMs can't be cold-initiated via API: only a private reply to a user's comment (one message, within 7 days) or a reply within 24h of the user's message.

recommendations: COMPLIANT SEQUENCE, step 0 (setup, week 0): Complete Meta Business Verification and display-name approval so the portfolio is no longer stuck at 250. Confirm the BSP (Fortius) is a Solution Partner or what billing mode applies, confirm INR migration of the WABA before 2026-12-31, and keep the BSP wallet funded so in-window replies and any billable utility templates don't silently fail. Prefer a dedicated outreach number, ideally a separate business portfolio from any critical customer-service number, because the limit and the 30-day restriction operate at portfolio level (my judgment, not Meta text).

Step 1 (Day 0, first touch, NOT WhatsApp template): Send a personalised email from the Ivinfotech domain (SPF/DKIM/DMARC set, plain text, one link). It carries their landing page, a 20-30s video link, and a wa.me deep link with prefilled text such as 'Hi, send me the demo for <Company>'. Do the same via their website contact form or a LinkedIn note when email is missing. Include a one-line unsubscribe. Do not use Instagram/Messenger cold DMs. The API doesn't allow them. Log every touch and its source URL in the CRM.

Step 2 (when the lead taps the wa.me link or replies): The inbound message opens the 24h window. The agent (rate-limited and task-focused) replies free-form: acknowledge, send the video (MP4 H.264/AAC under 16 MB) and landing page link, use up to 3 interactive reply buttons, and ask for explicit named opt-in, e.g. 'Reply YES to get updates and offers from Ivinfotech on WhatsApp. Reply STOP anytime.' Store opt-in text, timestamp, wamid and source in the CRM. Free-form replies are free up to 1,000 per number per month, then about Rs 0.115 each.

Step 3 (follow-up outside the window, only for opted-in leads): Use APPROVED MARKETING templates only (never disguised as utility). Template shape: a static opening word, a business name, one specific benefit tied to their landing page, a quick-reply button 'Interested' and a quick-reply 'Stop', and no variable at the start or end. Cap at one proactive template per lead per week and a maximum of 3 touches without a reply. Then mark the lead cold and stop. Budget about Rs 1.02 per delivered marketing template at Meta rates plus any BSP markup. Treat any inbound reply as a new window and let the agent continue free-form.

Step 4 (optional paid layer): Run Click-to-WhatsApp ads (interest/location/lookalike for Gujarat manufacturing and SMEs), plus a Custom Audience only from lists you have rights to (own CRM, inbound leads, prior clients). The ad click is a user-initiated chat and the FEP window makes replies free (assume 72h). Capture opt-in in the first thread and attribute via the webhook referral.ctwa_clid. Do NOT upload scraped numbers to Custom Audiences without confirming your rights position (Meta's terms require rights/permissions and a lawful basis).

RATE AND LIMIT ADVICE: Ramp slowly. Week 1 no more than 30-50 new recipients per day, then increase about 25-50% a day only while all templates are GREEN and the failed-status rate for codes 131049/131048/131050/131026 is low. Stay well below the tier limit, since unique recipients count outside windows per rolling 24h at portfolio level, and note Meta's scaling needs usage of at least half the limit over 7 days with high quality. Send in business hours IST only. Never retry 131049 within 24h. Do not resend a failed template to the same user. Auto-pause the whole campaign on any YELLOW/RED template, a phone-number quality drop, an account_alerts or account_update webhook, or any 131048. Keep the owner as final approver of template wording and the daily cap.

STOP / OPT-OUT HANDLING (build in the CRM webhook): (a) Treat a button payload or text of 'Stop', 'Unsubscribe', 'Not interested', 'Band karo', 'Nahi chahiye' or similar free text as an immediate opt-out. The classifier must err on the side of suppression. (b) Write to the suppression list before any reply is generated. (c) Within the new 24h window, send one free-form confirmation ('You will not receive further messages'). (d) Handle failed status 131050 and the user_preferences webhook as opt-out. (e) Treat a high-signal event like a user block as an opt-out too, even though I found no block webhook. Use sustained non-delivery as a proxy. (f) Never re-add suppressed numbers via a new scrape. Check the suppression list before every template send and before every ad Custom Audience upload.

IF THE OWNER STILL WANTS DIRECT COLD TEMPLATES TO PUBLISHED BUSINESS NUMBERS: That violates the opt-in text as written, and enforcement is reactive (blocks and reports). It is the owner's decision, not a safe default. If done anyway, use only a dedicated number and portfolio you can afford to lose, a verified business with an approved display name, a first message that names Ivinfotech and why you are writing and offers a one-tap Stop, at most 20-30 per day, a single send per lead with no automated reminders, and an immediate kill-switch on any quality signal. Never use this number for existing customers.

Verify before building: have the BSP show the live INR rate card and billing mode, confirm whether in-window utility templates are charged, and confirm the CTWA free-window length in Business Manager. Re-check the Meta pricing page in a real browser (not a text fetch), since the text-fetch copy is stale.
risks: POLICY/OPT-IN: Messaging scraped or published business numbers with marketing templates violates Meta's opt-in text. Blocks and reports drive restriction (1-3 day template block, then 5/7/30-day full block, then account lock, then permanent disablement). A permanent ban can bar the organisation from all future WhatsApp products. The number, the display name and possibly the whole business portfolio are at risk.

PORTFOLIO-LEVEL BLAST RADIUS: Messaging limits and some enforcement are per business portfolio, shared by all numbers. A burned cold-outreach number can restrict the number used for existing customers if both are in one portfolio.

TEMPLATE MISCLASSIFICATION: Submitting a cold intro as 'utility' triggers automatic re-categorisation, a rate limit, then 7/30-day template restrictions and a 30-day portfolio restriction. Misuse warnings remove advance notice.

PRICING DRIFT: The 2026-10-01 service-message and utility-in-window billing is new. Meta's developer pricing text served to non-browser fetchers is stale and contradicts the FAQ, so vendor blogs and my own tooling can give wrong answers. India rupee figures come from secondary sources. BSP markup and GST are extra. An unfunded wallet may stop delivery of billable in-window messages (vendor-reported, conflicting).
INR MIGRATION DEADLINE: India-billed WABAs must migrate to INR by 2026-12-31 or Meta stops delivering messages from 2027-01-01. A BSP-hosted WABA that misses this goes silent.

AI-TERMS: Meta Terms 4.7 allows business AI but gives Meta discretion over 'primary' use. An open-ended chat agent may be reclassified. Feeding WhatsApp message data into shared AI training breaches the terms.

DELIVERABILITY: Per-user marketing caps (error 131049) and users' 'Offers and announcements' / 'Not interested' settings reduce delivery for low-engagement recipients even with perfect compliance. Cold leads will have low read rates, which depresses template quality.

REGULATORY: DPDP core obligations apply from 2027-05-13 (owner phone numbers of sole proprietors are likely personal data). A TRAI draft (2026) may extend spam rules toward OTT apps. This is not final and I could not verify its content.
AGENT ERRORS: An LLM that replies after an opt-out, or says something misleading, creates complaints that directly lower quality. An opt-out classifier failure is the highest-impact bug.

result.summary: As of 2026-10-14 the practical limits on an agentic outreach system in India are mostly platform and contract rules, not statutes. (1) DPDP Act 2023: the Act and the DPDP Rules (G.S.R. 846(E), dated 13 Nov 2025) are only partly in force. The core duties (notice and consent, closed list of legitimate uses, security, breach reporting, erasure, rights, Rules 3 and 5-16) start 18 months after publication, about 13 May 2027. MeitY floated cutting this to 12 months (13 Nov 2026) in Jan 2026; I found no notified amendment as of 9-12 Oct 2026, so it could move at short notice. There is no B2B or business-contact carve-out and no 'legitimate interest' ground. The only relevant exclusion is s.3(c)(ii): data the person made public themselves, or that a law obliges someone to publish. It is untested, and no FAQ, Board ruling or enforcement exists. (2) TRAI TCCCPR (DLT, DND, headers, templates, 140xx series, A2P voice) regulates commercial communication over telecom Access Providers' networks, i.e. SMS and voice. It does not cover WhatsApp, email or social DMs. Telcos have asked for OTT coverage and MeitY started an OTT-spam consultation in 2025, with no outcome found. The 18 Sep 2026 Third Amendment adds that nothing in TCCCPR exempts a sender from DPDP duties. (3) India has no standalone anti-spam law (s.66A was struck down in 2015), so cold B2B email is lawful today. Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft rules are the real gate. (4) The binding constraints are platform terms. WhatsApp requires opt-in before any business-initiated message, so a cold marketing template to a scraped number breaches Meta policy even though it is not illegal. Google Maps, LinkedIn, Meta and X all prohibit scraping or automation. (5) Content: ASCI's AI-labelling guidelines (dated 17 Sep 2026) take effect about late Dec 2026 or 1 Jan 2027. Fabricated testimonials and deepfakes are prohibited even with a label. Personalised messages that replicate a real person's face or voice must be labelled. Separately, ElevenLabs free-plan audio cannot be used commercially, which matters for the existing Hindi voice-over. Method: Act text from the PRS Gazette copy, Rules text from the MeitY PDF, and TRAI and ASCI texts were read directly. Other items come from official pages or secondary sources and are marked. Nothing was installed, purchased, signed up for or sent. Public official PDFs were saved to the scratchpad only to read them. This is research, not legal advice.

findings.topic: DPDP status and dates as of 2026-10-14
findings.detail: Rules G.S.R. 846(E) are dated 13 Nov 2025 (PIB says notified 14 Nov, so the timeline may be off by a day). Rule 1: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 took effect on publication; Rule 4 (consent managers) one year after (about 13 Nov 2026); Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 eighteen months after (about 13 May 2027). Commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E) puts Act ss.1(2), 2, 18-26, 35, 38-43 and 44(1),(3) in force from Nov 2025, s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d) from Nov 2026, and the rest (ss.3-17 plus penalties machinery) from about 13 May 2027 (secondary tracker, computed dates). The Board exists in law (G.S.R. 844(E), 4 members), but as of Sept 2026 no Chair or Members were reported appointed and no enforcement has been reported. Jan 2026 proposal to shorten to 12 months (13 Nov 2026): feedback closed 4 Feb 2026, no amending notification found as of 9-12 Oct 2026. Until 13 May 2027 the older IT Act s.43A and SPDI Rules 2011 still apply (s.43A is omitted by DPDP s.44(2) only on commencement), so a published privacy policy is already expected of a body corporate that handles personal information. Design for DPDP now.

findings.topic: DPDP: does B2B outreach on public business contacts need consent or notice?
findings.detail: Text: 'personal data' is any data about an identifiable individual (s.2(t)). A sole proprietor's, partner's or director's name, mobile or email is personal data, and the Act has no business-capacity carve-out. Lawful bases are only consent (s.6, with a Rule 3 notice) or the closed list of 'certain legitimate uses' (s.7). There is no 'legitimate interest' ground, and s.7(a)-(i) contains nothing for marketing or B2B prospecting. s.7(a) covers data the person voluntarily gave for a specified purpose, so a lead who replies 'yes, send the sample' can be served for that purpose until they object. Exclusion s.3(c)(ii): the Act does not apply to personal data made or caused to be made public by (A) the Data Principal herself or (B) a person obliged by Indian law to publish it. Reading (my analysis; untested): data the owner published on their own website, own Google Business Profile or own social page fits (A). Statutory registers (MCA, GujRERA promoter data) plausibly fit (B). Aggregator or enrichment-tool data, guessed or bought emails, and anything we derive (replies, page-view events, scores, notes) is NOT covered. Clifford Chance warns that businesses relying on public information (crawlers, telemarketers) cannot assume exemption. The Minister of State said in Feb 2025 that scraping public data is governed by the IT Act and that DPDP requires consent for specified purposes, while lawyers called this conflation. No FAQ or Board decision resolves it.

findings.topic: DPDP: obligations and penalties that apply to Ivinfotech as Data Fiduciary (from ~13 May 2027)
findings.detail: Responsible for its processors (s.8(1)), and processors only under a valid contract (s.8(2)); this covers Apify, the BSP, ElevenLabs, kie.ai, any LLM API and hosting. Accuracy if data is used for a decision or disclosed (s.8(3)). Reasonable security (s.8(5)); Rule 6 minimum: encryption/obfuscation/masking/tokens, access control, logs and monitoring, backups, processor-contract clauses, and retention of logs and personal data for 1 year to detect breaches. Breach (s.8(6), Rule 7): tell each affected person without delay in plain language with a contact, tell the Board without delay, and give a detailed report within 72 hours; there is no harm threshold. Erase on consent withdrawal or when the purpose is no longer served (s.8(7)). Rule 8(3) separately requires retaining personal data, traffic data and processing logs for at least 1 year, then erasing. Publish contact details of a person who can answer questions about processing (s.8(9), Rule 9). Publish how to exercise rights and a grievance system that responds within 90 days (s.8(10), s.13, Rule 14). Rights: access, correction and erasure for people who gave consent, including under s.7(a) (ss.11-12). Consent requests need a stand-alone, itemised, plain-language Rule 3 notice, available in English or any Eighth Schedule language (Gujarati included), with withdrawal as easy as giving consent; the fiduciary bears the burden of proving notice and consent (s.5, s.6(1),(3),(4),(10)). Penalty ceilings: INR 250 cr for security failures, INR 200 cr for breach-notification or children's-data failures, INR 50 cr for other breaches (Schedule). There is no startup/MSME exemption in force: s.17(3) is only an enabling power and no notification was found.

findings.topic: TRAI TCCCPR scope: SMS and voice only; WhatsApp and email are not covered
findings.detail: TCCCPR 2018, as amended by the Second Amendment (12 Feb 2025) and the Third Amendment (18 Sep 2026), works through telecom Access Providers. Commercial SMS goes only through registered headers and DLT-registered content templates. Promotional voice goes only from 140xx numbers; service and transactional voice from 1600xx/1601xx. Preference (DND) and Consent registers apply. A sender not registered with an Access Provider is treated as sending UCC, with suspension or disconnection of its telecom resources. Promotional SMS must carry an opt-out; explicit consent for service messages lasts 7 days; consent cannot outlive the contract. Third Amendment (effective in tiers 30/60/90 days after 18 Sep 2026, so about 18 Oct, 17 Nov and 17 Dec 2026): defines A2P (software-initiated) voice calls, including robo and pre-recorded/AI voice, which must be pre-declared to the Access Provider or they count as UCC; AI/ML spam detection; an action threshold of 3 unique complaints plus an AI flag; and inquiry-based commercial communication for 7 days. It adds that nothing in TCCCPR exempts a Sender from DPDP duties. I found no provision extending TCCCPR to WhatsApp, RCS, email or social DMs. Telcos (Airtel, Jio, Vi) lobbied for OTT coverage in 2024-25. MeitY announced OTT/RCS spam stakeholder consultations in Apr 2025 (no outcome found). Stakeholder comments in the Third Amendment explanatory memorandum asking to extend TCCCPR to OTT platforms were not adopted in the operative text I read. Telecom Act 2023 s.28 empowers rules for prior consent to 'specified messages' (advertising goods or services), DND registers and reporting, and the broad 'message' definition could one day reach OTT or email; I found no notified rules doing so. Implication: WhatsApp-plus-email needs no DLT registration; adding SMS or any automated voice calls would. The 'not extended to OTT as of today' part rests on absence of evidence.

findings.topic: Cold B2B email in India and mailbox-provider rules (2025-26)
findings.detail: India has no standalone anti-spam statute. The IT Act has no spam provision, and s.66A, the old 'annoyance' offence, was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015). B2B cold email is therefore lawful today (this point rests on secondary legal sources), with consent expected under DPDP from ~13 May 2027 for personal emails not excluded by s.3(c)(ii). ASCI says it handles complaints about emailers and websites. Gmail, all senders: SPF or DKIM, TLS, valid forward and reverse DNS, RFC 5322 format, and Postmaster spam rate under 0.3% (aim for under 0.10%). Bulk senders (about 5,000+ messages/day to Gmail from a primary domain; status is permanent once reached) also need SPF+DKIM+DMARC (p=none is enough) with From-domain alignment. Marketing mail needs one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post to an HTTPS URL) plus a visible link, honoured within 48 hours. Since Nov 2025 Gmail ramps up temporary and permanent (5.7.x) rejections. Yahoo: SPF+DKIM, DMARC at least p=none, one-click unsubscribe, spam rate under 0.3%, unsubscribes honoured within 2 days. Outlook.com (over 5,000/day, from 5 May 2025): SPF+DKIM+DMARC (p=none minimum, aligned); failures go to junk and may be rejected with 550 5.7.515. Small volumes are not 'bulk', but the spam-rate and authentication basics apply to everyone, and a burned domain also hurts the main ivinfotech.com mail.

findings.topic: WhatsApp rules (the binding constraint on the WhatsApp channel)
findings.detail: Business Messaging Policy (last updated 23 Sep 2026): you may contact people only if they gave you their number or username plus separate opt-in permission. You choose the opt-in method and must comply with law. Opt-in must be clear about the business name and can be collected off-WhatsApp (website, SMS, IVR, paper). Business-initiated conversations only via approved templates. You must honour opt-outs 'on or off WhatsApp'. 'Do not spam, mislead or surprise people.' Users can block or report, and quality limits apply. Meta can limit or remove access and bar the organisation from future use ('messaging people at scale in an unauthorized manner'). Meta Terms for WhatsApp Business Platform (last modified 23 Sep 2026): no scraping of the platform; no tracking, building or augmenting profiles of individual users from platform data (thread content excepted); no using platform data to train or improve AI/ML models (anonymised, aggregated and derived data included; fine-tuning for your exclusive use is allowed); general-purpose 'AI Providers' are barred only where AI is the primary functionality (reported by TechCrunch for the Jan 2026 terms; a business-specific sales or support bot is not the target). Consumer WhatsApp ToS prohibits bulk, auto-messaging and non-personal use. Net effect: a cold marketing template to a scraped number is not illegal under TRAI, but it breaks Meta policy and risks quality drops, rate limits and a ban. Inbound-first flows (lead messages first, replies within the 24-hour window, Click-to-WhatsApp, web form with opt-in) are fine.

findings.topic: ACTION: collect contact details the business itself published (own site, own Google Business Profile, own social page) for one relevant B2B pitch => ALLOWED (low risk)
findings.detail: Likely outside DPDP via s.3(c)(ii)(A), since the Data Principal made it public. No Indian statute bars B2B outreach. Keep a provenance record (URL, time, tool), contact only the published business channel, and treat it as untested. Derived data we create (replies, events, scores) is inside the Act from May 2027.

findings.topic: ACTION: use statutory public registers (GujRERA promoter data, MCA/director data) as lead sources => ALLOWED with care
findings.detail: Strongest fit for s.3(c)(ii)(B) (a person obliged by law to publish), but the fit is my inference and has not been tested. The GujRERA endpoints are undocumented and may change. Use the data only for the register-linked business purpose, do not republish it, keep it out of logs and consoles (the 2026-10-09 session already hit a PII print), and respect sector rules for claims.

findings.topic: ACTION: bulk-scrape Google Maps listings (Apify) and store names, phones and addresses as a lead database => RISKY
findings.detail: Google Maps End User Additional Terms (modified 27 Jan 2026) bar copying content, mass download or bulk feeds, and building business-listing, mailing or telemarketing lists for substitute services. Maps Platform API terms (modified 26 Aug 2026, s.3.2.3) bar scraping, copying and saving business names and addresses, caching, and using the content to create or augment an advertising product or to train ML. So both the scraping route and the official-API route conflict with storing lead lists. Consequences are contractual and technical (IP blocks, ToS claims), not a specific Indian criminal law; the MoS has said scraping may engage IT Act s.43, which no court has applied. Mitigation: keep volumes low, treat Maps only as a pointer (place_id/name), take contact details from the owner's own site, and never copy reviews or photos.

findings.topic: ACTION: scrape LinkedIn (profiles, search, jobs) or automate LinkedIn connect/DM with bots or extensions => AVOID
findings.detail: The User Agreement (effective 3 Nov 2025) s.8.2 bans scraping tools, bots or unauthorised automation to access the service, add contacts or send messages, fake identities, and circumventing limits. LinkedIn's help page says violators' accounts get restricted. In hiQ v. LinkedIn (N.D. Cal., Nov 2022) the user-agreement scraping ban was held enforceable in contract, ending in a $500k consent judgment, a permanent injunction and destruction of the data and derived code. Manual human use of LinkedIn is fine.

findings.topic: ACTION: scrape Facebook/Instagram pages or groups, or auto-DM from them => scraping RISKY, auto-DM AVOID
findings.detail: Meta Terms (effective 1 Jan 2025) bar automated access or collection without prior permission. Meta's Automated Data Collection Terms (7 Oct 2024) need express written permission, forbid collecting non-public personal data and ignoring robots.txt, and bar onward transfer or sale. A US district court (Meta v. Bright Data, Jan 2024) held Meta's terms did not cover logged-out scraping of public data, but it is a first-instance US ruling, I could not confirm the appeal status, and it does not apply to logged-in scraping or to India. Messaging: Instagram's messaging API only lets you reply after the user messages first (24-hour window); Messenger allows promotional content only inside the 24-hour window, or as labelled Sponsored Messages; X likewise allows bot DMs only after the user DMs first. Click-to-Message ads are the clean route, because the lead starts the conversation.

findings.topic: ACTION: scrape Meta Ad Library to find advertisers => RISKY (tolerated signal, no personal-data harvesting)
findings.detail: The official Ad Library API covers ads about social issues, elections or politics and ads delivered in the EU and associated territories, so Indian commercial ads are only visible through the web UI. Automated collection of Meta products without permission is barred by the Automated Data Collection Terms, so scraping it conflicts with Meta's terms. Use it only as a business-level signal ('this firm runs ads to WhatsApp'), and take contacts from the firm's own published channels, not from Meta.

findings.topic: ACTION: scrape X or run X bots/auto-DMs => AVOID
findings.detail: X developer guidelines say use only the official API and that scraping or browser automation means permanent suspension. Bots may DM only after the user DMs first, with an easy opt-out; replies only if the user engaged first (max 1 per interaction); automated accounts must be labelled and linked to a human-managed account.

findings.topic: ACTION: buy or enrich contacts from third-party databases, or guess emails (name@company) => AVOID
findings.detail: Not covered by the s.3(c)(ii) exclusion, since neither the person nor a law made the data public. Provenance is unknown, so you cannot show notice or consent (s.6(10) burden), and s.8(3) accuracy applies. It also drives spam complaints and email blocklisting. Commentators expect brokered lists to be the first casualty of DPDP.

findings.topic: ACTION: first-touch cold email to a business's published address (identified sender, source line, opt-out), low volume, authenticated domain => ALLOWED
findings.detail: There is no Indian prohibition and no TRAI coverage. Meet the Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft authentication and unsubscribe rules above and honour opt-outs within 24-48 hours. From 13 May 2027, personal (non-excluded) emails fall under DPDP. Do not send to guessed or bought addresses, and keep complaint rates near zero.

findings.topic: ACTION: first-touch WhatsApp MARKETING template to a scraped or public number with no opt-in => RISKY (policy-breaking, not illegal under TRAI)
findings.detail: Violates Meta's opt-in requirement (above). Sanctions are user blocks and reports, quality-rating drops, send limits, and potentially removal of the WhatsApp Business account and a bar on the organisation, which would also kill the sales CRM's inbound channel. DPDP adds exposure from 2027. Compliant alternatives: email-first; Click-to-WhatsApp ads or website/QR opt-in; template only after opt-in evidence; or a human-initiated one-to-one contact (not automated; consumer WhatsApp bans bulk and auto-messaging).

findings.topic: ACTION: reply to a lead who messaged first (24-hour window), including AI-drafted or AI-sent replies, with human hand-off => ALLOWED
findings.detail: A user-initiated window allows free-form replies; business-specific AI assistants are not the target of Meta's AI-provider restriction (policy text is high-confidence; the AI-bot reading rests on press reports of Meta's statement). Identify the assistant as AI on first reply, offer a human, and honour STOP in any wording or language. A template quick-reply or tap ('Yes, send the sample') is a valid user-initiated response and must be handled. Lead replies are untrusted input and must not be able to alter suppression, tool permissions or data access (prompt-injection risk).

findings.topic: ACTION: follow up after a STOP, 'No', block or complaint => AVOID
findings.detail: WhatsApp requires honouring opt-outs on or off WhatsApp. DPDP s.6(4),(6) require withdrawal to be as easy as consent and processing to stop. Treat any hostile or complaint reply as a permanent do-not-contact across all channels.

findings.topic: ACTION: send SMS or make voice calls (including AI/auto-dialled voice) from the agent => AVOID unless fully DLT-onboarded
findings.detail: This is the one place TRAI applies: DLT principal-entity registration, registered headers and templates, consent and preference scrubbing, 140xx for promotional calls, and pre-declaration of A2P/robo/AI-voice calls (undeclared = UCC, leading to barring or disconnection of telecom resources). The user does not want calls, so keep SMS and voice out of scope.

findings.topic: ACTION: use WhatsApp conversation data to build lead profiles or train/fine-tune models for a shared 'learning loop' => RISKY / AVOID for model training
findings.detail: The WhatsApp Business Platform terms bar tracking, building or augmenting profiles of individual WhatsApp users from platform data (thread content excepted) and bar using platform data to train or improve AI/ML systems, including aggregated or derived data (fine-tuning solely for your own exclusive use is allowed). Keep learning at the level of campaign outcomes (rates, which signal combinations convert), not per-person profiling, and set the LLM provider to no-training and minimal retention (verify provider terms).

findings.topic: ACTION: personalised landing page and video naming the lead's own business and public project, on an unguessable noindex URL, no third-party logos => ALLOWED
findings.detail: Addressing the lead with their own public business details is low-risk. Keep claims conditional and substantiable (ASCI Code Ch. I: claims of objective fact must be capable of substantiation; no distortion by implication or omission). Include sender identity and an opt-out line. GA/GTM on lead pages is lawful today, but from May 2027 tracking tied to an identifiable lead's token is personal-data processing needing notice, so keep it minimal. This is my judgement.

findings.topic: ACTION: show a third party's brand, logo, project name, client testimonial or competitor comparison on a page => RISKY unless permitted and factual
findings.detail: ASCI Ch. I cl.3: no reference to a person or firm without permission if it gives an unjustified advantage. Ch.
