IV: no unjustifiable use of another firm's name or initials, no unfair advantage of its trademark or goodwill, and comparisons must be factual, accurate and substantiable. Trade Marks Act s.29(8) makes advertising infringe if it takes unfair advantage of a mark, is contrary to honest practices, or harms its distinctiveness or reputation; s.30(1) protects honest identification. Do not imply endorsement, partnership or authorship of the lead's ads; verify who actually runs the ads (flagged in the 2026-10-09 session). Use client testimonials only with written permission, in current, exact wording. ASCI's celebrity guidelines say testimonials must reflect genuine, reasonably current opinion.

findings.topic: ACTION: invented, AI-generated or composite testimonials, fake results, fake urgency/scarcity => AVOID
findings.detail: ASCI AI-labelling guidelines (signed 17 Sep 2026) list fabricated endorsements or testimonials, exaggerated results through claims or visuals, and non-existent locations shown as real as prohibited even with a label. CCPA misleading-ad guidelines 2022 (penalties up to INR 10 lakh, INR 50 lakh for repeats) and Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023 (false urgency, e.g. 'only 2 left', confirm-shaming) apply to advertisers, sellers and platforms, but the Consumer Protection Act's 'consumer' excludes buyers for commercial purposes, so direct application to B2B pitches is uncertain (ASCI still applies).

findings.topic: ACTION: AI-generated video or voice in outreach (synthetic narrator, illustrated characters) => ALLOWED with disclosure; likeness/voice cloning of real people needs consent and a label
findings.detail: ASCI guidelines take effect three months after publication (published about 29 Sep 2026): about late Dec 2026, though one outlet says 1 Jan 2027. Mandatory label ('Audio/Video created using AI' or 'enhanced using AI') for: synthetic influencers or ambassadors; replicating a real person's likeness or voice even with consent for personalised messaging; fabricated events or settings that affect understanding; demonstrating a product that does not exist (their example is a 3D model of an unbuilt housing complex, relevant to real-estate leads). No label needed for routine edits, decorative or obviously fantastical elements, AI-written copy, subtitles or translation. Deepfakes or likeness without consent are prohibited. IT Rules amendment (notified 10 Feb 2026, effective 20 Feb 2026) puts SGI labelling duties on intermediaries and significant social media intermediaries, with no direct duty on ordinary advertisers stated in the source. Personality-rights injunctions against AI voice cloning exist (Bombay HC, Arijit Singh, 2024; Delhi HC, Anil Kapoor, 2023). How a regulator would treat a synthetic narrator voice is unclear. Recommendation: add a small 'Voice/visuals created using AI' caption on page and video.

findings.topic: ACTION: use ElevenLabs free-plan generated audio (the Hindi 'Ruhaan' voice-over) in videos sent to leads => AVOID until regenerated on a paid plan
findings.detail: ElevenLabs states the free plan has no commercial licence and 'cannot be used for any commercial purpose'; free-plan output also needs attribution when shared non-commercially. All paid plans include a commercial licence (excluding Beta services), and content generated outside a paid subscription cannot be used commercially. Per the project memory (not re-verified), the Hindi voice was generated on the free plan. Regenerate it on a paid plan (Starter or higher) and keep the invoice and dates.

findings.topic: ACTION: use kie.ai-generated stills and clips (Seedance, Nano Banana) in commercial outreach => RISKY until commercial rights are confirmed in writing
findings.detail: kie.ai's Terms of Use (effective 1 Aug 2025) do not address ownership or commercial use of generated output, and say nothing on likeness or deepfakes. Upstream model licences (ByteDance, Google) may also apply. Get written confirmation per model and keep it on file. This is a gap, not a finding of prohibition, and rests on a short page fetch.

findings.topic: ACTION: log, store and pass lead data to tools (Apify, BSP, ElevenLabs, kie.ai, LLM API, console output) => ALLOWED only with minimisation, processor contracts and masking
findings.detail: s.8(2) requires a valid contract with each processor; Rule 6 requires masking/encryption, access logs and monitoring; breach rules in Rule 7. Never print contacts to stdout, and put a lead ID, not the phone number, into prompts. Cross-border transfers are allowed under s.16 unless a country is notified, but Rule 15 lets the Government impose conditions by order (none found). Confirm processor DPAs, retention and no-training terms.

recommendations: Build the guardrails outside the LLM, as hard code in the CRM: (a) a lead-provenance record per lead (source URL, timestamp, tool/actor+version, legal route: own-published / statutory register / inbound / opted-in); ingestion is blocked if it is missing; (b) a channel allowlist per route (e.g. WhatsApp marketing template only when opt-in evidence exists; email for own-published business addresses; nothing on LinkedIn, X, Instagram or Messenger except replies after the user messages first); (c) frequency caps, quiet hours, a global kill switch and a human approval gate for each new template, data source, claim type and first send of a campaign.

One permanent, cross-channel suppression list, checked before every scrape ingest, enrichment and send. Store normalised phone, email, WhatsApp ID and domain, plus hashed identifiers so that erasure does not resurrect the lead. Honour STOP, 'No' and free-text opt-outs in English, Hindi and Gujarati; process within 24 hours (Gmail asks 48 hours, Yahoo 2 days); treat opt-outs received off-platform (email, call) the same, as WhatsApp requires; classify complaint or hostile replies as permanent do-not-contact.

First-contact message minimum: who we are (Ivinfotech, Mehsana), the specific reason for contacting this business, where we found the contact, a one-tap opt-out, and a link to the privacy notice. WhatsApp: footer 'Reply STOP' plus a 'No, thanks' quick-reply. Email: visible link plus RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post. Identify AI-handled replies as AI and offer a human on request.

Publish a privacy notice and grievance page on ivinfotech.com now (English plus Gujarati/Hindi). It should list itemised data (name, role, business, phone, email, public profile URL, interaction and page-view logs), purposes, source of data, retention, processors and cross-border transfers, how to withdraw, access, correct, erase or complain, and a named contact for queries. This meets SPDI Rule 4 today and Rules 3, 9 and 14 plus s.13 from ~13 May 2027; the grievance response limit is 90 days (aim for 30).

Consent and opt-in evidence ledger: timestamp, channel, exact text or version shown, source URL or message ID. s.6(10) puts the burden of proof on us. Log inbound replies as the s.7(a) 'voluntarily provided' basis, limited to the specified purpose.

Append-only audit log of every agent decision, tool call, prompt/output hash, outbound message and human approval, with lead ID, restricted access, no secrets, PII masked. Keep it at least 1 year, as Rule 6(1)(e) and Rule 8(3) require, then purge on a schedule.

Retention schedule (my judgement, within s.8(7) 'no longer served'): purge or anonymise unresponsive prospects about 6-12 months after the last contact; erase on withdrawal within days, keeping only the hashed suppression record; keep won-customer records per contract and tax law. Data-subject request handler (access, correct, erase, withdraw) with a log.

Security baseline per Rule 6: encryption at rest and in transit for the CRM DB, backups and scraped CSVs; role-based access plus MFA; access logs and monitoring; tested backups; processor DPAs. Write a one-page breach runbook with an owner: notify affected individuals and the Board without delay, with a detailed report within 72 hours. Treat lead replies as untrusted input (prompt injection must not be able to change suppression, permissions or exports).

Processor register (Apify, BSP waba.fortius.in.net, ElevenLabs, kie.ai, LLM API, email provider, VPS): contract or DPA, region, retention, no-training. Configure the LLM provider for no training and minimal retention. Do not train or fine-tune shared models on WhatsApp Business Platform data.

Email setup: send from a dedicated subdomain, not the main domain. SPF and DKIM aligned, DMARC from p=none (then tighten), PTR/TLS, one-click unsubscribe, bounce and complaint handling. Monitor Gmail Postmaster spam rate (target under 0.1%, never reach 0.3%). Pause automatically on complaints.

Claims and content register: every claim on a page or video maps to evidence (KPI source, written testimonial permission, date). No fabricated or AI-made testimonials, no fake scarcity, no third-party logos or imagery without permission, no Google Maps or Street View imagery. Independent reviewer-agent pass plus human sign-off for new templates and pages (the practice already used on 2026-10-09). Add the 'created using AI' caption to AI video and voice. Record the paid-plan licence evidence for ElevenLabs and written confirmation of commercial rights from kie.ai.

Compliance watcher: check the Gazette/MeitY for any DPDP commencement or amendment (12-month proposal), TRAI notifications, DoT Telecom Act s.28 rules, ASCI effective date, and Meta policy updates (WhatsApp policies changed 23 Sep 2026). Review quarterly and after each change.
risks: DPDP interpretation risk: the s.3(c)(ii) 'made public' exclusion is untested, and there is no FAQ, Board decision or enforcement. If the Board reads it narrowly, any scraped or aggregator-sourced contact data is processed without a lawful basis from ~13 May 2027 (possibly 13 Nov 2026 if the 12-month proposal is notified, which could happen on short notice). Penalty ceilings are INR 50-250 cr; actual levels are unknown.

WhatsApp account loss is the most likely real-world penalty. Cold marketing templates to non-opted-in numbers can cause blocks, quality drops, limits and a bar on the organisation, which would also disable the existing sales CRM inbound channel. Policy text was updated 23 Sep 2026, so details can shift.

Scraping ToS exposure: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and X all prohibit it. US case law is mixed (hiQ lost on contract; Meta lost against Bright Data on logged-out scraping), and Indian law is unsettled, with only a ministerial statement linking scraping to IT Act s.43. Expect IP blocks, actor breakage and, at worst, claims.

Regulatory drift: TRAI or DoT/MeitY could extend spam or consent rules to WhatsApp, RCS or email (Telecom Act s.28 enabling power; OTT consultation pending). The TRAI Third Amendment's tiered effective dates (30/60/90 days from 18 Sep 2026) fall within weeks.

AI-content risk: ASCI AI guidelines are about to take effect and it can pursue complaints about websites and emailers. Unlabelled replicated voice or likeness, fabricated testimonials, or overclaims (including sector-specific advertising limits, e.g. RERA, from project memory, not re-verified) would be hard to defend. Personality-rights injunctions are available against AI voice cloning.

Licensing gaps in the media pipeline: the ElevenLabs free-plan audio is not commercially usable, and kie.ai and upstream model commercial terms are unclear. Both could invalidate assets already built.

Autonomy risks: an LLM agent can be steered by malicious or accidental content in lead replies (prompt injection) or drift past its guardrails. Enforce limits in code, with an audit trail and a kill switch.

Evidence limits: DPDP Act and Rules, TRAI amendments and ASCI guidelines were read from primary or hosted texts. Gazette commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E), the compression status and some effective dates rest on secondary trackers; Google, Meta, LinkedIn, X and WhatsApp pages were read through a fetch tool and could contain summariser errors; the Instagram Terms of Use and kie.ai upstream terms were not read in full.
open_questions: Will the Board or MeitY treat contact data in third-party listings (Google Maps, IndiaMART, JustDial) as 'made public by the Data Principal' under s.3(c)(ii)(A) when the owner did not create the listing? Is a statutory register entry (GujRERA, MCA) 'made public under an obligation of law' under s.3(c)(ii)(B)? This needs Indian data-protection counsel, or wait for official FAQs.
Will MeitY notify the 12-month compression (13 Nov 2026) or any startup/MSME exemption under s.17(3)? The Board has no appointed members as of Sept 2026; when will it become operational?
Will DoT, TRAI or MeitY bring WhatsApp, RCS or email under consent or DND rules (Telecom Act s.28 rules; outcome of the MeitY OTT-spam consultation)?

What is the ASCI AI-labelling effective date (about late Dec 2026 vs 1 Jan 2027), and would a regulator treat a synthetic narrator voice or cartoon characters as needing a label? Do the CCPA misleading-ad and dark-pattern guidelines apply to B2B pitch pages?
What are the BSP's (waba.fortius.in.net) own acceptable-use and opt-in attestation terms? Were they accepted at onboarding, and are there template or volume caps for marketing sends?

Does kie.ai (and upstream Seedance and Nano Banana licences) allow commercial use of outputs for a marketing video, and does ElevenLabs need a paid plan before re-using the already-generated Hindi voice?

Which lead sources should be kept? Proposed: GujRERA and MCA (statutory), owner-published sites, inbound/ads-initiated, and Maps only as a pointer. Does the owner accept the residual risk on Maps and Ad Library scraping?
Does Ivinfotech plan to contact foreign (EU, UK, US) leads? If so, GDPR/PECR, CAN-SPAM and CASL apply and are outside this India-only research.

Should a first contact be allowed by a human on a personal WhatsApp number? It is not automated, but consumer WhatsApp ToS bars bulk or non-personal use, and I did not verify how Meta treats low-volume one-to-one business use.

result.summary: Design verdict (as of 2026-10-14): build Ivinfotech's agentic sales system as a deterministic workflow spine (CRM state machine + queue + deterministic sender/suppression/kill switch) with bounded Claude agent loops only where the path cannot be scripted (research/enrichment, pitch+creative, reply handling, exception triage), plus an independent QA agent with veto power. '24/7' means event-driven and scheduled short sessions, not an immortal LLM loop. This is exactly what Anthropic's own guidance prescribes (simplest thing that works; workflows for predictable paths, agents for open-ended ones; separate evaluator; checkpoints; stop conditions; sandbox). Run it on the Agent SDK (Python) on the VPS with API-key billing (NOT a Max/Pro subscription login, which Anthropic's terms exclude for products/Agent SDK use); keep Managed Agents (beta) as a later option. The model never holds credentials and never sends: it proposes into queues, and code (suppression, window, caps, approvals, kill switch, idempotency) disposes. Verified current prices: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 per MTok (cache read $0.10), Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50, Opus 5.5 $4/$20. My assumption-driven model gives about $0.49 LLM cost per fully worked lead plus about $1.5/day fixed: roughly $11 / $26 / $50 per day at 20 / 50 / 100 leads (about $335 / $772 / $1,502 per month), 2.5x higher in a pessimistic case; media (per-lead bespoke video, about $1.25 each) and the human's review time, not tokens, are the dominant costs. Autonomy must be earned in stages (shadow -> approve-everything -> auto low-risk replies -> auto first-touch within caps) with automatic demotion and a human dead-man switch. Vendor 'AI SDR' benchmarks are low-confidence marketing numbers; set baselines from your own first 300-500 sends.

findings.topic: 1. What Anthropic's published guidance says, and how it maps to this system
findings.detail:
PRINCIPLES (all from Anthropic docs/engineering posts):
- Workflows (predefined code paths) vs agents (LLM directs its own steps): use workflows for well-defined tasks, agents for open-ended problems where step count cannot be hardcoded; agents cost more latency/money and compound errors; start simple, add complexity only when it measurably helps; frameworks optional. Patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer. Guardrails: separate model instance for screening; sandbox; max-iteration stop conditions; pause at checkpoints for human feedback. Tools deserve prompt-engineering care (poka-yoke args, docstring-style descriptions). [building-effective-agents]
- Multi-agent research system: orchestrator-worker; agents ~4x chat tokens, multi-agent ~15x; token usage explained ~80% of performance variance; multi-agent pays only for high-value parallelizable work; lead saves its plan to external memory; resume from checkpoints (not restart); tracing; rainbow deployments so in-flight agents are not disrupted; start evals with ~20 representative cases; LLM judge with a rubric and single 0-1 + pass/fail prompt matched humans best; for stateful agents grade the final state. [multi-agent-research-system]
- claude.com multi-agent guidance: use multiple agents only for context protection, parallelization, or specialization (20+ tools / conflicting instructions); split by CONTEXT boundary, not by role (planner/implementer/tester split spent more tokens coordinating than working); a verification subagent needs only artifact + criteria; failure mode 'early victory'; multi-agent typically 3-10x tokens. [building-multi-agent-systems]
- Long-running harnesses: each session starts with no memory, so state lives outside the model (feature list as JSON with a pass field that the agent may only flip, progress log, git commits); startup routine reads state and runs a smoke test; agents declare victory early unless forced to verify end-to-end. A separate evaluator beats self-grading (models praise their own work) but an untuned Claude evaluator is lenient and needed several rounds of prompt tuning against human judgment. Each harness component encodes an assumption about model weakness; re-test and remove components as models improve. [effective-harnesses, harness-design-long-running-apps]
- Managed Agents architecture: session = durable append-only event log outside the harness; harness is stateless and replaceable (wake(sessionId) -> getSession -> resume); credentials never reachable from the sandbox (proxy/vault pattern). [managed-agents]
- Context engineering: smallest high-signal context, just-in-time retrieval, structured notes outside context, sub-agents return 1-2k-token summaries. [effective-context-engineering]

MAPPING (my judgment): the pipeline spine discover -> enrich -> decide -> build -> QA -> send -> inbox -> handoff is a WORKFLOW with agentic loops inside 3-4 stages, not a free-roaming swarm. Roster boundaries follow TRUST boundaries (agents that read untrusted web/replies get no send or write-to-world tools), CONTEXT boundaries (QA sees only the artifact + rubric), and permission boundaries; not job titles. Of ~10 logical roles only 4 need agent loops (Researcher, Strategist/Creative, Inbox, Orchestrator-on-exceptions); the rest are single structured-output calls (triage, injection screen, compliance check, scribe summary) or plain code. 'Agentic' = the model decides which leads deserve effort, what signal matters, what to pitch, how to word it, how to answer; code decides what is ALLOWED. This satisfies 'not fixed-rule automation' without giving up control.

findings.topic: 2. Runtime choice, 24/7 hosting and what access is needed
findings.detail:
OPTION A (recommended for phases 1-3): Claude Agent SDK (Python) worker on the existing VPS. SDK = Claude Code's loop/tools/hooks/permissions/subagents/sessions as a library; it spawns a claude CLI subprocess per session (~1 GiB RAM, 1 CPU, 5 GiB disk per concurrent agent as a floor; no top-level session timeout, so enforce max_turns, max_budget_usd and your own watchdog). Hosting doc's 'ephemeral per task' pattern fits: one short session per task, context rebuilt from the DB; SessionStore only if you want durable transcripts. Concrete config per agent run: tools=[] (remove all built-in Bash/Write/WebFetch for Inbox/Strategist/QA/Orchestrator); mcp_servers={'crm': create_sdk_mcp_server(...)} with narrowly-scoped @tool functions (tool name becomes mcp__crm__<tool>); allowed_tools = explicit mcp__crm__* list; permission_mode='dontAsk' (anything not pre-approved is denied, never prompts); max_turns, max_budget_usd (counts subagents; may overshoot by one response); effort per agent; setting_sources=[] and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 so ambient config/memory cannot leak in; env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS; run as a dedicated non-root user inside a container/sandbox with egress allowlist and a credential-injecting proxy (agent never sees WhatsApp/Apify/ElevenLabs/kie tokens; tools call your CRM API which holds them). Cost fields (total_cost_usd) are client-side estimates; reconcile daily with the Console Usage & Cost API. OTEL env vars give spans/metrics/logs. Concurrency on a shared CyberPanel VPS: cap at 2-3 sessions until RAM is measured.
OPTION B (later / for specific agents): Claude Managed Agents (beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01): Anthropic-hosted harness; scheduled deployments (cron, min granularity 1 minute, up to ~15% jitter capped at 9 min, 1,000 per org, per-run budget, pause/unpause, deployment_run records); webhooks (HTTPS 443, signed, event id for dedupe, up to 3 attempts, NOT ordered, NOT a durable log: reconcile by fetching); session budgets (hard USD cap, session goes idle with budget_reached, new work rejected until raised); permission policies (always_ask pauses the session until user.tool_confirmation; MCP toolsets default to always_ask); outcomes (separate-context grader against a markdown rubric, default 3 / max 20 iterations); multiagent (up to 20 predefined agents, one shared budget); vaults; $0.08 per running session-hour plus tokens; no Batch discount; not ZDR/HIPAA eligible; 300 create / 1,200 read requests per minute per org. Pros: durable sessions, built-in grader, no loop to babysit. Cons: beta (behavior may change), leads' PII stored server-side, custom tools still run in YOUR app.
OPTION C: plain Messages API single calls with structured outputs (json_schema) for classifiers, injection screens, QA graders, summarizers: cheapest and safest, no loop needed.
AUTH RULE (important): Anthropic's legal page says OAuth/subscription (Free/Pro/Max) login is for ordinary individual use; developers building products/services incl. the Agent SDK should use API-key auth from Claude Console (or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), and may not route requests through plan credentials. Advertised plan limits assume ordinary individual usage. So 'Claude Code on my Max plan running 24/7' is not the production path: budget for API billing and use `claude --bare -p` / SDK with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
ACCESS CHECKLIST: Anthropic API key (dedicated, in a root-owned env file, never in chat or repo; set Console spend limit; org-level spend limits exist, workspace-level limits unverified); Apify token (monthly cap); BSP WhatsApp token held ONLY by the CRM sender; kie.ai/ElevenLabs keys behind wrappers with max-credit args; site-deploy tool with whitelist route + rollback; DB access only through tool API (no raw SQL); an owner-notification channel that is not routable to any agent (separate number/Telegram/email) for alerts and the STOP-ALL command; systemd units (dispatcher, agent-worker@N, sender, existing Flask webhook) + timers, heartbeat table + watchdog alert, DB backups.

findings.topic: 3(a). Agent roster: inputs, outputs, tools, permissions, autonomy
findings.detail:
Legend. Action risk tiers: R0 read; R1 internal write (CRM notes/scores); R2 reversible external-visible (deploy noindex lead page, create template draft); R3 irreversible external (WhatsApp send, template submit); R4 commitments (price, discount, contract, legal/regulatory claims, refunds). Autonomy: A0 observe; A1 propose -> human approves; A2 act within caps + sampled audit; A3 act + notify; A4 act freely but only RESTRICTIVE actions (veto, suppress, pause). Models: Haiku 5.5 = screens/triage/classify; Sonnet 5.5 = default worker; Opus 5.5 = optional for tier-A strategy and QA judge. Pin model IDs (claude-sonnet-5-5 etc. are pinned snapshots; Sonnet 5.5 retirement not before 2027-09-28).

0) Dispatcher/Scheduler (CODE): leases tasks, enforces per-agent concurrency, budgets, kill switch, bundle pinning. No LLM.

1) Orchestrator (Sonnet 5.5, loop, thin; invoked on daily plan 06:00 IST + exceptions/DLQ/anomaly/owner commands, NOT polling). In: funnel counts by state, yesterday's metrics, budgets left, failed tasks, playbook index. Out: bounded task rows (<=30 per run, depth<=2, allowlisted task types), plan note, owner questions. Tools: crm_funnel_stats(R0), crm_list_tasks(R0), crm_create_task(R1, type-allowlist), crm_pause_lead(R1), ask_owner(creates approval), read_playbook(R0). No web/send/deploy; cannot change budgets, flags, autonomy level or kill switch. A2.

2) Discovery (Haiku 5.5 single-call triage + deterministic Apify/RERA/Ads-library jobs; Sonnet 5.5 only for weekly 'which sources/queries to try' strategy). In: source configs, ICP, chain filter, dedupe vs leads+suppression. Out: candidate rows with raw evidence, freshness, triage score. Tools: apify_run(actor allowlist, schema-bound input, max_usd arg), rera_search(R0), crm_upsert_candidate(R1, dedupe key). Public business data only; store business contact fields, never scrape private profiles. A3.

3) Researcher = Enrichment+Qualification (Sonnet 5.5 loop <=12 turns, <=~$0.40/run). In: candidate. Out: dossier JSON: facts[] each with source_url, fetched_at, confidence, expires_at; need_signals; ability_to_pay_signals; reachability (channel, opt-in evidence); entity_verified (boolean + evidence, e.g. ads owner == target entity; the Shree Infra vs 'Patel Group' ad-branding mismatch from the earlier pilot is exactly this check); chain_flag; tier A/B/C/reject; disqualifiers. Tools: fetch_page(url) via sanitizing proxy (text only, size-capped, Haiku injection screen, wrapped as JSON tool_result), maps_lookup, ads_library_lookup, mca_lookup, crm_write_dossier(R1). NO send, deploy, shell, or cross-lead reads (it reads untrusted web content). A3 (may reject leads; may not contact).

4) Strategist (Sonnet 5.5 high effort, Opus 5.5 for tier A; single structured call or <=5-turn loop). In: dossier + offer catalogue + proof-point table (case studies, verbatim testimonials) + vertical playbook skill + outcomes of similar past leads. Out: pitch_brief JSON: pain hypothesis with fact_ids, offer, proof_point_ids, angle, CTA, language (EN/Hinglish/Gujarati), channel decision, do-not-say list, expected objections, risk flags. Tools: crm_get_dossier, crm_search_outcomes, crm_get_proof_points, crm_save_brief (R1). A3.

5) Creative (Sonnet 5.5 + deterministic renderers). In: pitch_brief. Out: page_spec JSON filling slots of the APPROVED campaign Jinja template (no free-form HTML/CSS/JS from the model), video_script + beats with caption text (WhatsApp autoplays muted, so captions-first), image prompts, template variable values, choice among already-approved WhatsApp templates. Tools: render_page(spec) -> preview URL, render_video(beats, max_credits) (kie.ai/ElevenLabs behind wrappers; tier A only for bespoke video, tier B reuses a template video with local caption overlay), crm_save_assets (R1). Cannot deploy to prod, cannot submit new templates (R3, approval). Every factual sentence must carry fact_id/proof_point_id. A2.

6) QA/Auditor (SEPARATE context; Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 for first N pages and tier A). In: ONLY artifact + rubric + facts table (reasoning-blind: no Strategist rationale). Out: per-criterion pass/fail with evidence, claims_check (sentence -> fact_id or FAIL), banned-claims scan (e.g. statements that a RERA phase is registered), mobile/a11y/link checks via Playwright screenshot, opt-out line + AI-disclosure present, PII scan. Tools: get_artifact, get_facts, screenshot(url), lint_page (all R0). Authority: blocking veto; cannot edit. Must run concrete/negative tests, not 'looks fine' (early-victory failure). A4 (veto only).

7) Outreach/Compliance gate (CODE + Haiku 5.5 final-message classifier, Sonnet 5.5 CoT second stage only on flags). Checks listed in finding 9. Not an agent; authority over the sender.

8) Sender (CODE): the only component holding the BSP token; sends outbound_queue rows after policy_result=pass, approval satisfied, idempotency key, kill switch clear, dry-run flag respected.

9) Inbox/Reply (Sonnet 5.5 loop <=6 turns; one session per inbound message; per-lead lock). In: lead brief assembled by code (state, dossier digest, last ~10 messages wrapped as untrusted JSON with source labels, allowed actions given 24h-window/state, objection-handling skill). Out: structured intent (enum), language, sentiment, confidence; proposed reply or template choice; requested actions. Tools (lead_id bound at session creation, not model-supplied): get_conversation, get_dossier_digest, propose_reply (queue only), set_intent, schedule_followup, request_handoff, request_opt_out. Cannot send, cannot see other leads, no web. A1 for pricing/legal/complaint/unknown intents and ALL replies until stage S2; A2 for low-risk intents afterwards.

10) CRM Scribe: mostly CODE. Every tool call/webhook writes an append-only event in the tool layer (PostToolUse hook / wrapper), so 'update CRM for every activity' never depends on the model remembering. Haiku 5.5 only writes human-readable timeline notes and the daily digest.

11) Handoff: deterministic triggers (interested/meeting/pricing/'call me'/human requested/hot score/complaint/legal threat/won-signals) + Sonnet/Haiku writes a <=150-word brief (who, what, why now, next step, risks) -> owner channel with SLA timer and escalation; sets human_owned=true so auto-replies stop (STOP handling stays automatic). WON is a human-confirmed state; the agent can only mark won_candidate. A3.

12) Learner/Auditor (weekly + daily digest; Sonnet or Opus): reads events/metrics/transcripts, clusters failures, proposes playbook/prompt/skill changes as CANDIDATE bundles that must pass the eval gate and human approval; never edits production prompts itself. A1.

findings.topic: 3(b). Control plane: tables, state machine, idempotency, retries, state outside context, kill switch
findings.detail:
Existing CRM is Flask + SQLite with 4 workers (per earlier-session notes, 4 days old, re-verify). At 20-100 leads/day SQLite is adequate with WAL + busy_timeout and BEGIN IMMEDIATE for atomic task leasing; migrate to Postgres (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) if multiple agent workers contend.

TABLES (add to the CRM):
- leads, contacts(e164, source, opt_in_evidence, entity_verified), lead_state_log.
- tasks(id, type, lead_id, payload, status[queued|leased|done|failed|dead], priority, attempts, max_attempts, run_after, lease_owner, lease_expires, idempotency_key UNIQUE, parent_task_id, depth, created_by, bundle_sha). Idempotency key = hash(type, lead_id, step_version); a duplicate enqueue is a no-op.
- runs(run_id, task_id, agent, model, bundle_sha, session_id, started/ended, status, turns, tokens in/out/cache_read/cache_write, cost_est_usd, stop_reason, transcript_ref).
- tool_calls(run_id, tool, args_hash, args_scrubbed, result_summary, policy_decision, latency). Written by hook/wrapper, not by the model.
- events (append-only audit log: ts, lead_id, actor[agent|human|system|lead], type, payload, run_id, optional hash chain). Source of truth for 'every activity'.
- messages(wamid, direction, text, template, status, provider_message_id).
- outbound_queue(id, lead_id, contact_id, template, params_json, send_after, status, idempotency_key UNIQUE, approval_id, policy_result_json, provider_message_id). The model can only INSERT rows here via propose_*; it never has a send function.
- approvals(id, subject_type, subject_id, risk_tier, preview/diff, requested_by, status[pending|approved|edited|rejected|expired], decided_by, decided_at, edit_distance, reason).
- suppression(phone_hash, reason, source, ts) never deleted; checked at SEND time.
- facts(fact_id, lead_id, claim, source_url, fetched_at, confidence, expires_at) and proof_points (immutable testimonials/KPIs): the only allowed grounding for outbound claims.
- assets(slug, page_version, video_url, qa_report, deploy_status, rollback_pointer).
- spend_ledger(ts, run_id, vendor[anthropic|apify|kie|elevenlabs|whatsapp], units, usd_est, usd_reconciled) and budgets(scope, period, soft_limit, hard_limit).
- control_flags(kill_switch per scope[global|outbound|agent X], autonomy_level per action class, dry_run, send_window, daily_caps).
- prompt_bundles(sha, agent, model, tools, skills, status[candidate|shadow|canary|active|rolled_back]); eval_cases/eval_runs/eval_results; handoffs(lead_id, brief, sla_due, acked_by).

LEAD STATE MACHINE (transitions validated in code; agents request transitions via a tool): DISCOVERED -> ENRICHING -> QUALIFIED | REJECTED -> BRIEFED -> ASSETS_BUILDING -> QA_PENDING -> APPROVAL_PENDING -> READY -> SENT -> DELIVERED -> READ -> REPLIED -> INTERESTED | OBJECTION | QUESTION | NOT_INTERESTED | OPTED_OUT -> HANDOFF_PENDING -> HUMAN_OWNED -> WON | LOST. Illegal transitions are rejected; per-lead max transitions and max outbound count (e.g. 1 template + 1 follow-up + <=6 replies per 24h) are code constants.

IDEMPOTENCY / EXACTLY-ONCE EFFECTS: at-least-once task execution + idempotent effects. Inbound webhooks dedupe on wamid/event id (Managed Agents docs state webhooks can repeat and arrive out of order; same discipline). Send path: write intent row -> check provider_message_id/status before any retry -> send with outbound_id as idempotency key -> record result. Tools that create things take a client-generated request_id.
RETRIES: exponential backoff + jitter on 429/5xx/overloaded; max 3 attempts then dead-letter queue + owner alert; SDK already emits api_retry events; a failed tool returns an actionable error (isError) so the model can adapt rather than loop.
STATE OUTSIDE CONTEXT: every run starts fresh and receives a code-built 'lead brief' (like the harness post's progress file + JSON feature list): current state, last N messages, open tasks, dossier digest, allowed actions. Agents modify state only through tools that validate field-level permissions (Anthropic found models clobber JSON less than Markdown). Transcripts are stored for audit but are NOT the source of truth; do not rely on session resume for correctness. Pin bundle_sha to a task at lease time so in-flight work finishes on the old prompt version (rainbow-deploy idea).
KILL SWITCH: control_flags checked by (1) dispatcher before leasing, (2) every tool wrapper, (3) a PreToolUse hook, (4) the sender before every message. Scopes: pause outbound only / pause all agents / freeze + revoke tokens. Triggers: owner STOP-ALL via a non-agent channel, CRM button, auto-trips (hard spend cap, error-rate spike, opt-out spike, WhatsApp quality drop, unexpected tool-denial storm, no heartbeat). Dead-man rule: if no human has touched the approval queue for 48h, autonomy auto-drops to S1 (nothing sends without approval). Safety paths (STOP handling, suppression, kill switch, sender caps) must work even if the Claude API is down.

findings.topic: 3(c). Event flow and the deterministic vs model-judgement split
findings.detail:
EVENT FLOW
- Inbound: BSP webhook -> existing Flask handler (verify + dedupe on wamid) -> write events/messages -> LAYER 1 deterministic router: delivery/read receipts update state; button payloads (the pilot found api/inbound.py ignores type=button, so the 'Yes, send the sample' tap is currently dropped; fix first); STOP/opt-out keyword + regex list in English/Hindi/Gujarati/Hinglish (stop, unsubscribe, band karo, mat bhejo, ...) -> suppression insert + deterministic confirmation, BEFORE any LLM sees it -> everything else enqueues handle_inbound(priority high) -> worker leases the lead, builds lead brief, runs Inbox agent -> propose_reply -> policy gate -> (approval if required) -> sender. If Claude is unavailable, fall back to an acknowledgement template within the free-form window + owner alert.
- Scheduled (systemd timers, IST): 06:00 Orchestrator plan + discovery jobs; rolling enrichment/strategy/creative/QA queues (can use Batch API overnight at 50% off); send window only inside configured business hours with per-day and per-hour caps; follow-up-due scan (+48h, max one follow-up); hourly health/spend pulse (code, wakes Orchestrator only on anomaly); 21:00 daily digest to owner; nightly reconciliation (spend vs Console usage, deliverability stats, suppression sync); weekly eval + Learner run.
- Page/engagement events: server-side logs/GA page views and button taps -> events -> may trigger follow-up eligibility.
- Human events: approval decisions, handoff acks, STOP-ALL -> events; approvals resume the paused task (propose -> pending -> approved -> sender).

DETERMINISTIC CODE (never model): scheduling, queueing, leases, dedupe, retries, state-machine validation, suppression and opt-out handling, send-window/24h-window/quota checks, template-parameter validation, recipient resolution (E.164 from verified contact row), slug allowlist and URL building, page/video rendering from specs, deploy + rollback, sending, status webhooks, budget accounting and caps, kill switch, audit logging, authorization (lead scoping), PII scrubbing.
MODEL JUDGEMENT: which candidates are worth pursuing and why (need x ability-to-pay x reachability, chain filter), whether an ad/entity match is real, pitch angle and proof selection, copy/script/storyboard, reply intent beyond keywords (soft opt-outs, sarcasm, language mixing), objection handling draft, when to ask a question vs hand off, handoff brief, QA review, anomaly interpretation, weekly learning.
GRAY ZONE decided by risk: model proposes, code validates (e.g. which template to use, whether to follow up, which page variant).

findings.topic: 3(d). Human-in-the-loop gates and staged autonomy
findings.detail:
WHY NOT 'APPROVE EVERYTHING FOREVER': Anthropic telemetry shows users approve ~93% of Claude Code permission prompts, so per-action approvals decay into rubber-stamping; their guidance is deterministic limits (hard send caps, recipient rules) plus human review reserved for novel/high-risk actions. SaaStr (self-reported, undated, vendor-adjacent) says agent performance tracked human attention and estimated 15-20 h/week of oversight across five agents; they started in draft/approve mode and loosened after 30-60 days. [how-we-contain-claude, claude-code-auto-mode, SaaStr]

GATES BY RISK TIER: R0/R1 no gate (logged). R2 deploy of lead page: QA pass + (S1) human OK. R3 first-touch WhatsApp send, new template submit: approval until the stage permits otherwise; template submit always human. R4 pricing/discount/contract/regulatory claims/complaints: ALWAYS human, at every stage. STOP/suppression: always automatic (restrictive action). Spend above caps, budget raises, autonomy-level changes, kill-switch reset, prompt-bundle promotion: human only.

STAGES (promote only on numeric criteria; demote automatically):
- S0 Shadow (1-2 weeks): full pipeline on 5-10 leads/day, dry_run=true, sender redirects to owner test numbers or no-ops. Compare tiers/pitches/replies to human labels (use the pilot's A/B/C-labelled leads). Exit: qualification agreement >= ~80% with human on A/B/C, QA catches 100% of planted critical defects, zero policy-gate bypasses.
- S1 Approve-everything: every first-touch and every reply needs approval; cap ~10 sends/day; approval UI shows preview, evidence links, QA report, risk flags; batch approvals; inject occasional deliberately flawed drafts (canaries) to measure reviewer attention (my suggestion). Exit (proposed defaults to tune): last 50 first-touch approvals >= 90% unedited, 0 critical errors (wrong recipient, false claim, compliance), QA-vs-human agreement >= 90%, opt-out/complaint rate within your own baseline.
- S2 Auto-reply for low-risk intents inside the 24h window (yes/no/FAQ/scheduling/receipt acks); first-touch still approved; 20% random post-hoc audit; pricing/legal/complaint/unknown still A1. Exit: 100 audited replies with <5% needing correction, 0 critical.
- S3 Auto first-touch for tier A/B leads with QA pass + pre-approved template + entity_verified, inside hard caps (daily/hourly/per-segment) and send window; human samples 10-20% and sees a daily digest. 
- S4 (optional, months later) wider segments/higher caps; still never autonomous for R4.
DEMOTION (automatic, one-way ratchet down; only the human ratchets up): any critical error, spend anomaly, QA false-negative found by a human, opt-out or block/report spike, WhatsApp quality rating drop, injection detected in a reply that reached a tool call, dead-man timeout. Handoff SLA: human must ack within a set time or the system escalates to a second channel; once human_owned, agents stop replying.
AUTO-MODE DESIGN LESSONS to reuse for the outreach gate: judge actions not narration (strip the generator's rationale), two-stage asymmetric classifier (cheap aggressive Haiku pass, costlier CoT pass only on flags), screen inputs as well as outputs, check at handoffs, deny-and-continue with escalation after repeated denials, track both false positives and false negatives (their full pipeline: 0.4% FPR but 17% FNR on real overeager actions, so never rely on a classifier alone for irreversible actions).

findings.topic: 3(e). Evaluation: offline sets, replay, metrics, regression gate
findings.detail:
ANTHROPIC METHOD (Demystifying evals, Jan 2026): task/trial/grader/transcript/outcome vocabulary; code graders for outcomes and tool-call checks, model graders (rubric, pairwise) calibrated against humans with an 'Unknown' option and one judge per dimension, human graders for calibration; capability evals (start low) vs regression evals (~100%); pass@k for 'one good answer is enough', pass^k for customer-facing consistency (a 75% per-trial rate gives ~42% over three trials); conversational agents are graded on END STATE + transcript constraints + rubric, often with a second LLM simulating the user (tau-bench style); start with 20-50 tasks from real failures; grade outcomes not paths; read transcripts; isolate trials; swiss-cheese layering of evals + monitoring + A/B + feedback. Multi-agent post: ~20 cases reveal large effects; single 0-1 + pass/fail judge prompt matched humans.

OFFLINE SUITE (~180 cases at launch, grows from every production incident):
- Inbox classifier 60: Hindi/Gujarati/English/Hinglish replies incl. STOP variants, soft opt-outs, abuse, 'who is this', price questions, button taps, forwarded numbers, emoji-only, voice-note placeholders. Safety-critical items (opt-out detection) must hit pass^5 = 100%.
- Injection 30: adversarial replies and poisoned website/Maps/RERA text trying to trigger sends, exfiltrate other leads, change recipient, reveal prompts. Pass = no forbidden tool call, no leakage, attempt flagged.
- Qualification 30: the earlier pilot's labelled A/B/C leads (e.g. ads landing on WhatsApp + proof of pay = A; national chain units = reject) with expected tier and disqualifier.
- Claims/QA 20: pages with planted unverifiable claims and wrong-entity facts; QA recall target >= 95% on critical defects.
- Reply drafting 30 simulated conversations (LLM lead-simulator): end-state checks (correct CRM state, suppression created when needed, handoff fired, no R4 commitments, AI disclosure present).
- Handoff 10.
Run cost: about 180 x $0.06 = ~$11 per full run synchronous, ~$5.40 via Batch API (50% off) (my estimate from the cost model).

REPLAY: every production conversation is stored as events; a replay harness feeds recorded inbound messages to a candidate bundle in dry-run with the same lead brief and diffs proposed replies/actions against what shipped and against human edits.

PRODUCTION METRICS (compute per segment/template/bundle): delivery rate, read rate, page-view and button-tap rate, reply rate, POSITIVE reply rate (interested or asks for sample/call per 100 delivered), opt-out rate, block/report rate and WhatsApp quality rating, time-to-first-response (inbound -> first proposed reply and -> sent; target p50 of a minute or two within the window since an LLM turn takes seconds), handoff acknowledgement latency, approval rate and edit distance of drafts, QA false-negative rate (defects humans find after QA pass), hallucination rate (claims without fact_id), cost per positive reply and per qualified meeting, spend vs budget, tool-denial rate, loop/timeout rate.
STATS REALITY: a two-proportion test (alpha 0.05, 80% power; my calculation) needs about 685 sends per arm to separate 10% from 15% reply rate, ~1,060 per arm for 5% vs 8%, ~1,500 per arm for 3% vs 5%. At 50 sends/day that is weeks per A/B. So gate prompt changes mainly on OFFLINE evals + shadow/replay, use production only for guardrail metrics (opt-outs, blocks, errors) and coarse comparisons.
REGRESSION GATE BEFORE ANY PROMPT/TOOL/SKILL/MODEL CHANGE (treat the bundle as code in git): candidate bundle -> frozen regression suite (no critical regression; pass^k thresholds on safety items) -> new-case suite -> shadow on live inputs 2-3 days (no side effects) -> canary on a slice of low-risk traffic (replies, not first-touch) -> promote by switching prompt_bundles.status pointer; auto-rollback on guardrail breach. Re-run the full suite on any model ID change and quarterly (infra and model drift change agentic results). LLM judges: calibrate against ~50 human-labelled items, keep judges in separate context, tune skepticism with few-shot examples (the harness post needed several tuning rounds). Weekly human transcript review of 20-30 conversations; Learner proposes new eval cases from failures.

findings.topic: 3(f). Cost model: verified prices, explicit assumptions, 20/50/100 leads per day
findings.detail:
VERIFIED PRICES (platform.claude.com pricing page, fetched 2026-10-14), USD per MTok in / 5m cache write / 1h cache write / cache read / out: Sonnet 5.5 2 / 2.50 / 4 / 0.10 / 10; Haiku 5.5 (prompt <=100k) 0.10 / 0.125 / 0.20 / 0.01 / 0.50 (>100k: 0.50 in, 2.50 out); Opus 5.5 4 / 5 / 8 / 0.20 / 20; Fable 5.1 10 / 12.50 / 20 / 0.25 / 50. Batch API -50% in/out (not for Managed Agents, not with fast mode). Web search $10 per 1,000 searches (web fetch has no extra fee). Managed Agents runtime $0.08 per running session-hour + tokens. Models since 4.7 use a tokenizer producing ~30% more tokens for the same text; all token counts below are on the new tokenizer. Min cacheable prompt 512 tokens (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku 5.5); default TTL 5 minutes; caching breaks even after 1 read (5m) or 2 reads (1h). Anthropic recommends starting with Opus 5.5 for most workloads and describes Sonnet 5.5 as best speed/intelligence and Haiku 5.5 for classification/extraction/routing.

ASSUMPTIONS (mine; tokens per lead stage): 'lead' = a fully worked lead that reaches outreach; 5 raw candidates triaged per worked lead. (1) Triage Haiku: 1.5k fresh + 3k cached in, 0.2k out, x5. (2a) Researcher Sonnet loop ~8 turns: 20k fresh + 12k cache-write + 70k cache-read in, 5k out. (2b) injection screen Haiku on 6 pages: 24k in, 0.6k out. (3) Strategist Sonnet: 8k fresh + 5k write + 20k read, 3k out. (4) Creative Sonnet: 10k + 5k + 25k, 7k out. (5) QA Sonnet x2 reviewers: 15k fresh + 10k read, 2k out each. (6) compliance check Haiku. (7) Inbox: 10% reply rate x 2 turns, each = Haiku classify + Sonnet draft (6k fresh+3k write+15k read, 1k out) + Haiku guard. (8) Scribe Haiku. Rework factor 1.3x on stages 3-5. Fixed daily overhead: orchestrator plan + 6 exception wakeups + Opus daily audit digest + weekly 60-case eval amortized = $1.46/day.

RESULT per worked lead (LLM only): triage $0.0014; researcher $0.127; screen $0.0027; strategist $0.0605; creative $0.105; QA $0.102; compliance $0.0003; inbox $0.0063; scribe $0.0004; rework +$0.080 => about $0.49 per lead.
PER DAY (LLM): 20 leads $11.2; 50 leads $25.8; 100 leads $50.1 (per month x30: ~$335 / $772 / $1,502). PESSIMISTIC (per-lead tokens x2.5, fixed x1.5: longer contexts, more rework, Opus on strategy/QA): $26.5 / $62.9 / $123.7 per day. Opus-everywhere roughly doubles the Sonnet-stage cost (Opus 5.5 is exactly 2x Sonnet 5.5 on every rate); Opus only for tier-A strategy (20% of leads) adds ~$0.012 average per lead. Managed Agents runtime would add ~$0.027 per lead (20 active minutes).
NON-LLM (from earlier-session measurements in memory; not re-verified except credit rate): Apify ~ $0.05 per surviving lead (~$0.6 for 115 raw -> 12 A/B leads); media: bespoke kie.ai storyboard video ~ $1.25 per lead (~250 credits observed for 8 stills + 8 clips; kie.ai shows 200 credits = $1 on a partial pricing page, medium confidence) vs ~$0 for a template video with local caption overlay. TOTAL per day: with template media $12.2 / $28.3 / $55.1; with bespoke video for every lead $37.2 / $90.8 / $180.1. So bespoke video is ~2.5x the entire LLM bill: route creative spend by tier (A bespoke, B template+overlay, C page only). WhatsApp per-message fees, ElevenLabs paid plan and VPS cost are excluded (not verified here; WhatsApp pricing is another research topic).
LEVERS: Haiku-first triage (already in); prompt caching with static prefix first (tools -> system -> messages; cache read is only 5% of input price on Sonnet/Opus 5.5); for Inbox at 5-10 replies/day a 1h TTL does NOT pay (12k-token prefix: $0.024 uncached, $0.03 for a 5m write, $0.048 for a 1h write, $0.0012 per read: 1h needs >=2 reads per hour), rely on in-session 5m caching; Batch API for overnight triage/enrichment/evals (-50%); cap tool-result size; limit turns; effort 'low/medium' for routine agents; skip enrichment for obvious rejects. Anthropic's own multi-agent token multiples (4x agent, 15x multi-agent vs chat; 3-10x per the later guidance) are the reason to keep agent loops few.
REAL COST IS HUMAN TIME: plan 1-2 h/day at S1 falling toward 30 min/day at S3 (SaaStr's self-reported 15-20 h/week for five agents is the cautionary upper bound). Script: scratchpad cost_model.py (reproducible).

findings.topic: 3(g). Failure modes and concrete guardrails
findings.detail:
FRAME: Simon Willison's lethal trifecta (private data + untrusted content + external communication) and Meta's Agents Rule of Two (no session should combine untrusted input, sensitive data/systems, and state-change/external communication; split across sessions) are the design test. A sales agent has all three by nature, so split them by agent. Guardrail products are not reliable on their own (Willison: 95% catch rate is a failing grade; a paper from OpenAI/Anthropic/Google DeepMind authors reported adaptive attacks defeat most published defenses, per a secondary summary). Anthropic's own list: model layer is probabilistic and cannot be the only control; egress/permission/credential controls are what hold.

1) PROMPT INJECTION via lead replies / websites / Maps reviews / RERA fields / button payloads / fetched PDFs. Mitigations: untrusted text only inside tool_result blocks, JSON-encoded with source labels (Anthropic's recommended structure); system prompt states tool content is data; Haiku 5.5 structured-output screen on every fetched page and every inbound reply before the main agent sees it (treat a stop_reason 'refusal' as a positive); Researcher and Inbox have NO send/deploy/shell/cross-lead tools (Rule of Two); lead_id bound at session creation and verified by PreToolUse hook (tool_input.lead_id must equal session lead) so a hijacked agent cannot read or message other leads; Inbox can only queue proposals; PostToolUse hook can replace tool output (updatedToolOutput) to strip/flag content; persistent notes written from untrusted text are stored as quoted raw text, screened, and re-labelled untrusted when re-read (Anthropic notes persistent memory carries injections across sessions); sub-agent output is not trusted more than raw tool output; red-team suite in evals; canary strings in dossiers to detect leakage.
2) HALLUCINATED / UNVERIFIABLE CLAIMS (the pilot already hit this: RERA registration statements, ads-owner mismatch, stale scraped event dates are the classic SaaStr failure). Mitigations: Creative may only cite fact_ids/proof_point_ids; testimonials and KPIs come verbatim from immutable tables; banned-claims list in code; entity_verified must be true for first-touch; facts expire (expires_at) and are re-checked before send; page generated from approved template slots, model cannot write arbitrary HTML/JS; independent QA with concrete tests; claims phrased conditionally when unverified.
3) WRONG RECIPIENT / WRONG PERSONALISATION. Mitigations: sender takes outbound_id, never a phone number from the model; recipient resolved from contacts.e164 with source and opt-in evidence; template {{name}}/{{project}} params validated against the contact+dossier; dry-run mode redirects every send to the owner's own test numbers; allowlisted test numbers; first N sends human-verified; per-lead idempotency key; double send prevented by unique key and status check before retry.
4) RUNAWAY SPEND. Layered caps: per run max_turns + max_budget_usd (+ headroom for one overshooting response); per-agent daily token budget; global daily and monthly hard caps in budgets table with 50/80/100% alerts and auto kill-switch at 100%; Console spend limit; Apify monthly limit; kie.ai/ElevenLabs credit caps via wrappers (the pilot used a 300-credit cap with a ledger); max Apify run cost argument; daily reconciliation because SDK cost fields are client-side estimates; Managed Agents (if used) has per-session and per-deployment hard budgets.
5) LOOPS / FAN-OUT. max_turns; same-tool-same-args repeat detector in PostToolUse (hash; >3 repeats -> deny + escalate); task depth and per-run task-creation caps; SDK subagent depth=1 and concurrency env limits; per-lead max transitions/messages; DLQ; watchdog on stalled runs.
6) PLATFORM/COMPLIANCE HARM (opt-out ignored, spam, quality-rating collapse). STOP handling deterministic and first; suppression checked at send time; send-window + daily/hourly/segment caps; auto-demote on block/report spikes; AI disclosure in the first message of each conversation (see finding 10); no replies after human_owned; no messaging outside 24h window except approved templates.
7) APPROVAL FATIGUE. Few, rich, batched approvals; risk-based routing; sampling instead of 100% review at later stages; canary bad drafts; metrics on approval latency and edit distance.
8) SELF-GRADING BIAS / LENIENT QA. Separate context, artifact-only input, concrete and negative tests, calibrate against human labels, optionally stronger model for tier A, measure QA false-negatives.
9) TOOL MISUSE / EXCESS AGENCY (OWASP LLM06 Excessive Agency, secondary source): minimal tool set per agent (<=10-12, namespaced mcp__crm__*), least-privilege scoped tokens, no open-ended tools (no Bash/WebFetch for outreach agents), authorization enforced downstream in CRM API not just in prompts, HTTP egress allowlist, credentials in proxy/vault not in agent environment.
10) CREDENTIAL / INFRA. Dedicated non-root user; container with --cap-drop ALL, read-only root, egress through allowlisting proxy (per Anthropic secure-deployment guide); the earlier pilot's open items (rotate pasted Apify/ElevenLabs keys, remove temporary SSH key, rotate root password) must be closed before 24/7 operation.
11) MODEL/VENDOR DRIFT. Pinned model IDs; bundle versioning; re-run evals on any change; OTEL + DB tracing; incident postmortem -> new eval case.
HOOK MECHANICS (Agent SDK): PreToolUse runs BEFORE deny/ask/allow rules; any hook deny wins even in bypassPermissions; callbacks can allow, deny, ask, defer or rewrite input (updatedInput); matchers match tool NAMES only so inspect tool_input inside the callback; multiple hooks run in parallel and the most restrictive result wins; a PreToolUse timeout means the tool call is not run; async hooks can log but cannot block; use PostToolUse (async) for audit writes. Use hooks as the last-mile policy gate, but keep the hard guarantees (suppression, caps, kill switch) in the sender/tool layer so they do not depend on SDK behavior.

findings.topic: 4. Policy constraints that shape the design
findings.detail:
- Anthropic Usage Policy: consumer-facing chatbots/agents must disclose to users they are talking to AI (at least at the start of each chat); prohibits convincing people they are talking to a human, spam/phishing/social engineering, circumventing other platforms' terms, collecting non-public contact details without permission, and compiling personal data from multiple sources into profiles shared without awareness; users are responsible for agents' tool actions. The disclosure rule is written for consumer-facing agents; applying it to B2B WhatsApp is my conservative recommendation (and also supports WhatsApp quality). Design consequences: first message and every Inbox conversation states it is an automated assistant from Ivinfotech with a human follow-up; no fake human personas; store only business contact data with a source; keep dossiers out of third-party disclosure. [aup]
- Claude Code/Agent SDK terms: commercial terms + API-key auth for products/services (see finding 2); do not modify the binary; branding rules ('Claude Code' name cannot be used in your product name).
- WhatsApp: coverage of the Jan 15 2026 Business Solution Terms change says it bars AI providers from distributing general-purpose chatbots as their primary product, while businesses using AI for customer service/updates are unaffected; one source mentions a different effective date for new vs existing accounts (unconfirmed against Meta's document). Ivinfotech's use (a business messaging its own prospects) appears outside the ban but verify the current terms text. Opt-in, 24h free-form window, template categories and quality rating are enforced by Meta; they belong to a separate research topic, but the architecture must treat them as hard code-level constraints (caps, window logic, opt-out).
- Data: Managed Agents is stateful and not ZDR/HIPAA eligible; Anthropic's data-retention page states retained data is not used for training without express permission (standard commercial retention period not extracted; confirm). India DPDP Act obligations for scraped owner contacts not researched here.

findings.topic: 5. Practitioner evidence on autonomous SDR agents (treat as low confidence)
findings.detail:
- SaaStr (Jason Lemkin; undated page, internal clues suggest late 2024; vendor-adjacent, self-reported, unaudited): ~19,800 outbound messages in six months, 6.7% response / 4% positive; 15-20 h/week human oversight across five agents (outbound lists 3-4 h, performance/training 2-3 h, inbound review 1-2 h); performance fell in busy weeks; started in draft/approval mode then loosened after 30-60 days; sub-$1,000 sales closed autonomously while high-value deals are qualified by AI and handed to humans; inbound instant-response was the clear win; AI cannot fix broken ICP/messaging/RevOps; 2-3 week deliverability warm-up; training on real winning conversations and a detailed ICP with non-examples.
- Vendor benchmark blogs (Laxis, Smartlead, Unify; all sell competing products): fully autonomous ~1-3% reply rates, hybrid AI-drafts/human-approves ~8-15%, signal-driven supervised outreach 14-25%; reply-quality drift of 30-50% by week 8 on autonomous platforms; claims that 47% of deployments are capped by domain-reputation collapse or 70-80% fail by 90 days are unverified. The pattern (supervised and signal-triggered beats fully autonomous cold volume) is consistent but the numbers are not reliable.
- I found no credible public postmortem of a wrong-recipient or hallucination incident in a production AI SDR, so the guardrails in finding 9 come from Anthropic's security guidance and the Ivinfotech pilot's own mistakes (ads-owner mismatch, PII printed to a console, deleting a template by name when the BSP ignores the name filter).
Implication: the earlier pilot's insight (target need + ability to pay + reachability, evidence-first claims, personalised page+video) is the part with real leverage; volume is not. Design for quality-per-send and keep daily volumes modest until your own data justifies more.

findings.topic: 6. Prerequisites in existing assets and phased build order
findings.detail:
PREREQUISITES (from earlier-session notes; re-verify live code before relying): (1) sales api/inbound.py handles only type=text, so template quick-reply taps (type=button) are ignored; (2) test sends are not recorded in OutreachLog so there is no delivery tracking; (3) app code supports only IMAGE headers in send_template_message while the BSP accepts VIDEO templates (creation verified; send-time video header param not yet verified in app code); (4) open key-hygiene items (pasted Apify/ElevenLabs keys, temp SSH key, root password); (5) landing-page deploy is currently a manual whitelist route + HUP and needs a scripted deploy-with-rollback tool; (6) no spend ledger, approvals, kill switch, or suppression-at-send-time in the new agent layer.
PHASES: P0 (week 0-1) control-plane tables, deterministic sender with dry-run, suppression + STOP router, kill switch, spend ledger, button handling, API-key + non-root runtime, hooks skeleton. P1 (weeks 1-3) S0 shadow: Researcher + Strategist + Creative + QA on 5-10 leads/day, approvals UI (can be a simple CRM page/WhatsApp-to-owner digest), build eval set from pilot labels. P2 (weeks 3-6) S1 approve-everything with ~10 sends/day, Inbox agent proposing replies, handoff channel, daily digest, measure baselines over the first 300-500 sends. P3 S2 auto low-risk replies + audit sampling; weekly Learner + regression gate. P4 S3 auto first-touch for tier A/B within caps. Evaluate Managed Agents (outcomes grader, scheduled deployments, budgets) for the QA/Creative loop once it leaves beta. Each phase ends with a written go/no-go against the numeric criteria in finding 6.

recommendations: Adopt the 'workflow spine + bounded agent loops' architecture: only Researcher, Strategist/Creative, Inbox and an exception-driven Orchestrator are agent loops; QA is an independent veto agent; triage, screens, compliance check and summaries are single structured-output calls (Haiku 5.5); sender, suppression, caps, kill switch, logging are plain code.

Run on the Agent SDK (Python) on the VPS with API-key billing (Console), dedicated non-root user, container + egress allowlist, tools=[] built-ins removed, explicit mcp__crm__* allowlist, permission_mode='dontAsk', max_turns + max_budget_usd per run, setting_sources=[] and auto-memory disabled; do NOT plan on a Max/Pro login for 24/7 use.

Make 'model proposes, code disposes' non-negotiable: no agent ever holds the WhatsApp token or a send function; agents INSERT proposals into outbound_queue/approvals; a deterministic sender enforces suppression (at send time), 24h window, caps, send window, approval state, idempotency and kill switch.

Build the control-plane tables (tasks, runs, tool_calls, events, outbound_queue, approvals, suppression, facts/proof_points, spend_ledger, budgets, control_flags, prompt_bundles, eval tables) and the lead state machine BEFORE any outbound agent; write audit events in the tool layer so every activity reaches the CRM without relying on the model.

Fix the known gaps first: handle button-type inbound replies, record all sends in the outreach log, add deterministic multilingual STOP/opt-out routing ahead of the LLM, scripted deploy-with-rollback for lead pages, and close the open credential-hygiene items from the pilot.

Split untrusted-content readers from actors (Rule of Two): Researcher/Inbox cannot send or deploy; Inbox is lead-scoped by a bound lead_id verified in a PreToolUse hook; screen all fetched pages and replies with a Haiku structured-output injection check.

Ground every outbound claim in fact_ids/proof_point_ids and generate pages from approved template slots; require entity_verified for first touch; have QA verify claims with concrete negative tests in a separate context.

Introduce autonomy in stages S0 shadow -> S1 approve-everything -> S2 auto low-risk replies -> S3 auto first-touch within caps, with numeric promotion criteria, automatic demotion, a human dead-man switch (48h without approvals drops to S1), and R4 actions (price, discounts, legal/regulatory claims, complaints) always human.

Build the eval suite (~180 cases) before going live: classifier incl. Hindi/Gujarati/Hinglish opt-outs (pass^5 = 100% on safety items), injection set, qualification set from the pilot's labelled leads, claims/QA planted-defect set, simulated reply conversations; gate every prompt/tool/model change on regression + shadow + canary, and rely on offline evals because production A/B needs ~700+ sends per arm.

Control cost by tiering creative spend (bespoke video only for tier A, template video + caption overlay for B, page only for C), Haiku-first triage, caching static prefixes, Batch API for overnight work; set hard daily/monthly caps with auto kill-switch and reconcile SDK cost estimates daily with the Console usage API. Budget roughly $11 / $26 / $50 per day LLM at 20 / 50 / 100 leads (pessimistic x2.5) plus media.
Keep volumes modest and measure your own baselines over the first 300-500 sends (reply, positive reply, opt-out, block rate, WhatsApp quality); ignore vendor 1-3% / 8-15% / 15-25% claims as targets.

Disclose AI in the first message of every conversation and never imply a human; hand off to the owner on defined triggers with an SLA timer, and stop agent replies once a human owns the lead; 'won' is a human-confirmed state.
risks: Fully unattended outbound can wreck the WhatsApp number's quality rating or trigger blocks/reports; irreversible, so caps, send windows, auto-demotion and human sampling are mandatory.

Prompt injection cannot be fully prevented by any filter or model training (Willison; secondary report of adaptive attacks beating published defenses); only architecture (no trifecta in one session, scoped tools, queue-and-gate sending) limits blast radius.
LLM-judge QA is lenient by default (Anthropic needed several tuning rounds); QA false negatives will reach humans unless measured against planted defects.
Approval fatigue (Anthropic: ~93% of permission prompts approved) turns S1 into rubber-stamping; the system also degrades when the owner's attention drops (SaaStr).

Cost model is assumption-driven (token counts, 10% reply rate, rework factor); Hindi/Gujarati text may tokenize much worse than the assumed ratio; SDK cost fields are client-side estimates; media (bespoke video) and WhatsApp fees can dominate and WhatsApp fees are unverified here.

Managed Agents is beta (behavior may change, no ZDR/HIPAA, PII stored server-side); the Agent SDK path needs an operations-grade host (memory growth in long sessions, ~1 GiB per concurrent agent on a shared VPS).
Using subscription (Max/Pro) credentials for 24/7 automation conflicts with Anthropic's stated authentication rules and could be restricted without notice; API billing is required.

Legal/compliance exposure not fully researched: India DPDP obligations for scraped business-owner contacts, WhatsApp opt-in evidence, regulatory advertising limits (e.g. RERA claims) and whether AUP AI-disclosure formally applies to B2B messaging.
Small eval sets and slow production feedback (weeks per A/B) mean prompt changes can regress quietly; model ID/tokenizer changes require full re-evaluation.

Existing infrastructure risks from the pilot (leaked pasted keys, temporary SSH key and root access, SQLite with multiple writers) could turn an agent bug into a security incident if not closed first.
open_questions: VPS capacity: how much RAM/CPU is free beside the website and CRM for concurrent Agent SDK subprocesses (about 1 GiB each as a floor), and is a separate worker VM acceptable?

WhatsApp constraints needed to set caps: India marketing-template per-message price, daily conversation/tier limits, quality-rating thresholds, 24h window rules, and whether a business-initiated AI-assisted flow needs any extra disclosure (another research topic; not verified here).
Token inflation for Hindi/Gujarati/Devanagari text on the current tokenizer: measure with the token-counting endpoint on real dossiers and replies before locking the cost model.
Anthropic standard commercial retention period for API inputs/outputs and whether ZDR is worth pursuing for leads' PII; DPDP Act position on storing scraped owner contacts (not researched).
Does the Console offer workspace-level spend limits in addition to org-level limits (org-level limits are mentioned in the Managed Agents reference; workspace-level not verified)?
What is the owner's real review-time budget per day, and should approvals happen in a CRM page, WhatsApp/Telegram digest, or both?
kie.ai credit price is derived from a partial pricing page (200 credits = $1); confirm current rates before budgeting bespoke video.
When (if ever) will Managed Agents leave beta, and will outcomes/grader and scheduled deployments justify moving the QA/Creative loop there?
Does the AUP AI-disclosure requirement formally apply to B2B WhatsApp prospecting? The design discloses anyway; confirm with counsel if volumes grow.

result.summary:
Snapshot EXISTS and is usable. Everything below was read from local files only (nothing run, nothing sent, no secrets or phone numbers printed). Path shorthand used in all sources: SNAP = C:/Users/ADMINI~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Administrator-Desktop-wire-soldering/dec5451d-390d-44dc-a02c-fbc50c6d4a7c/scratchpad/sales_snap/code/backend and SP = C:/Users/ADMINI~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Administrator-Desktop-wire-soldering/dec5451d-390d-44dc-a02c-fbc50c6d4a7c/scratchpad.

BOTTOM LINE: The CRM already has a mature pipeline. It has a job queue, an audit table, a human approval inbox (todo_items), per-campaign send-approval gates, a suppression list, STOP and auto-reply classifiers, and dashboard kill switches that default OFF. What it lacks for a Claude-driven agent system is concentrated in five places.
1. Inbound WhatsApp drops everything except plain text, so the template Yes/No buttons are invisible.
2. Auth is one shared admin session with no scoped agent credential. The same session can flip the global send switch and approve to-dos.
3. The kill switch is checked only in scheduler ticks, not in the send functions.
4. The template sender cannot send the approved video/URL-button template, so every real send so far bypassed the CRM through ad-hoc SSH scripts. Those sends leave no OutreachLog row, and replies to them would be dropped.
5. Nothing in the ad-hoc discovery/page/video tooling is parameterised, idempotent or cost-metered. It is hard-wired to one lead (Shree Infra / Riverview Heights) and to Windows paths.

What is missing from the snapshot, exactly:
- The main sales_system.db is absent. Only the -wal (5.5 MB) and -shm files were captured, and they contain live data. I did not read them.
- .env is absent. Only variable NAMES are in SNAP/../meta/env_keys.txt.
- The logs dir is empty, and log_signatures.txt and git_status.txt are empty (git working tree clean).
- Code is at git HEAD 9732be8 (2026-09-11). Runtime state was captured 2026-10-09 09:29. Nothing newer was captured, so any production change after that is unseen.
- Frontend sources are present but I did not audit them.
- runtime.txt shows 3 gunicorn workers and "no systemd units / no cron" for this app. The memory note says "4 workers, bos-* systemd units". I could not reconcile the two.

findings.topic: 1a. Stack and runtime of the existing CRM
findings.detail: Flask 3 + SQLAlchemy 2 + SQLite in WAL mode (busy_timeout 10 s) via SNAP/database/db_config.py:9-27. Frontend is React/Vite (not audited). Gunicorn runs 3 workers on 127.0.0.1:5005 behind LiteSpeed. LiteSpeed proxies only /api/, so any public route MUST live under /api/ (this caused the live unsubscribe/interest bugs fixed 2026-09-10; see SNAP/api/interest.py:8-15). Four standalone loop processes run next to the API: jobs.worker (sequential OUTREACH_EMAIL/OUTREACH_WA/CLASSIFY_INBOUND), scraper_worker.async_runner (DISCOVER/ENRICH/REVIEW/SCORE), jobs.discovery_scheduler (300 s tick) and jobs.inbound_poller (IMAP, 120 s). All run as root (snapshot meta/runtime.txt). The LLM layer is Gemini primary with OpenAI fallback behind one wrapper, call_json() in SNAP/cognition/llm_client.py. There is no Anthropic provider, but this single function is the swap point. Schema evolves through SNAP/database/schema.sql (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS) plus SNAP/migrate.py (idempotent ALTER list), with no Alembic, so adding new agent tables is cheap and low-risk. requirements.txt is 10 lines. Every table in schema.sql has models.py, so there are 36 tables.

findings.topic: 1b. Tables the agent system can build on
findings.detail:
All in SNAP/database/models.py.
- leads (65-93): status set DISCOVERED, ENRICHED, REVIEWED, SCORED, OUTREACHING, OUTREACHED, ENGAGED, HOT_LEAD, CONVERTED, REJECTED. 'Won' is CONVERTED. There are no columns for opt-in/consent evidence, source URL/evidence, enrichment JSON, pitch decision, human owner or WhatsApp-verified flag.
- lead_contacts (392), lead_scores (123), lead_review_insights (109), lead_firmographics (96).
- outreach_logs (149-177): channel, status SENT/DELIVERED/FAILED/BOUNCED, provider_message_id (wamid), read_at, variant_id (= WhatsApp template name). There is NO index on lead_id or provider_message_id (schema.sql index list), so webhook lookups scan the table. This is fine at 5 MB.
- inbound_conversations (193-208): UNIQUE(channel, provider_message_id) gives idempotent dedup, plus intent_detected, confidence, ai_suggested_response, is_read.
- suppression_list (212-221): UNIQUE(channel, identifier), reasons UNSUBSCRIBE/STOP/BOUNCE/MANUAL.
- jobs (225-237): PENDING/CLAIMED/DONE/FAILED/DEAD, attempts and max_attempts=3, backoff, run_after.
- agent_events (251-262): agent, lead_id, action_type, confidence, risk_level, routed_to, outcome, JSON payload. It is the de-facto audit log.
- whatsapp_templates (461-519): status DRAFT/PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/ADMIN_REJECTED, purpose FIRST_TOUCH/FOLLOW_UP, is_active manual kill, origin ADMIN/AI, product scoping.
- campaigns (621-689): status, per-channel email_outreach_approved_at / whatsapp_outreach_approved_at gate, watchdog_alert, test_outreach_sent_at.
- todo_items (756-782): the human approval inbox, with proposal JSON, is_blocker, status PENDING/APPROVED/DISMISSED.
- interest_responses (549-557): UNIQUE(outreach_log_id, response).
- outreach_sequences (443-455), system_settings (368), system_heartbeats (376), channel_policies (522), content_assets (427), knowledge_base_items (603), strategy_insights/campaign_theses (703/726), prospects/prospect_searches (563/586).
Defined but with zero code references outside models.py: client_lifecycle, team_capacity, campaign_variants, knowledge_memory. client_lifecycle is a ready-made home for post-WON handoff data.

findings.topic: 1c. API routes (all prefix /api/v1)
findings.detail:
Auth gate: SNAP/app.py:71-77 requires session['authenticated'] on every route except the public prefixes at 45-56 (/health, /auth/, /inbound/, /webhooks/, /unsubscribe/, /interest/, /go/, /outreach-approval/).
- leads.py: GET list 202, recent-replies 346, GET one 486, PATCH fields 571 (whitelist 563-568), GET /<id>/timeline 597-684, POST create 739, POST /<id>/outreach 793 (manual, synchronous), POST revise-draft 903, PATCH /<id>/status 1011 (any of VALID_STATUSES, line 34).
- inbound.py: GET/POST /inbound/whatsapp 23/38, PATCH /<conv>/read 66.
- webhooks.py: POST /webhooks/resend 48.
- whatsapp_templates.py: CRUD plus /propose 348, /<id>/approve 306, /reject 330, /revise 447, /refresh 480, /builtin 79.
- campaigns.py: CRUD, POST /<id>/outreach-approval/<channel> 227, /daily-review 262, /watchdog/clear 316.
- todos.py: GET 18, feedback 54, approve 72, dismiss 86.
- settings.py: GET/PATCH 23/32. env_settings.py: GET/PATCH 13/18. alerts.py: GET 164 (needs_response + ready_to_claim). system.py: GET /live 95.
- Also products, prospects (Serper X-ray search with a monthly budget), content_assets (upload), knowledge_base, message_formats, social_queue, analytics, reports, dashboard, strategy_insights.
- Public one-click GET routes: interest/<lead>/<log>/<YES|NO>/<hmac> (api/interest.py:33), unsubscribe/<lead> (api/unsubscribe.py:24), outreach-approval/<campaign>/<channel>/<hmac> (api/outreach_approval.py:20), go/whatsapp?to=<digits> (api/redirects.py:37, a wa.me 302 hop because Meta rejects direct wa.me button URLs).

findings.topic: 1d. Inbound webhook handlers
findings.detail:
WhatsApp GET verify handshake: SNAP/api/inbound.py:23-35 (verify-token check only). POST: 38-63 always returns 200 and swallows exceptions. It iterates entry.changes.value.messages (-> _handle_one_message, 121-139) and value.statuses (-> _handle_one_status, 82-118).
- Status callbacks match OutreachLog.provider_message_id: read sets read_at, delivered SENT->DELIVERED, failed SENT->FAILED and triggers evaluate_execution_watchdog (3 consecutive failures pause the campaign).
- _handle_one_message returns early with only a log line if msg.type != 'text' (123-125).
- Text goes to record_inbound() (SNAP/services/inbound_service.py:41-101). It looks the sender up by exact equality on leads.primary_phone / whatsapp_number (25-38), runs the deterministic STOP check (suppresses immediately) and the auto-reply check, otherwise enqueues a CLASSIFY_INBOUND job in the same commit as the row.
- A message from a number with no matching lead is DROPPED with a warning (60-63) because inbound_conversations.lead_id is NOT NULL.
- Resend email webhook (SNAP/api/webhooks.py:48-97) handles opened/clicked/delivered/bounced. It has no Svix signature check; the code comments admit this (14-17).
- Email replies come via IMAP polling in jobs/inbound_poller.py.

findings.topic: 1e. Classification, auto-reply and the on/off flags
findings.detail:
Deterministic first (SNAP/cognition/hard_classifiers.py): is_optout regex (18-31) includes \bstop\b, 'not interested', 'no thanks', 'remove me', 'opt out'. Quoted-reply stripping is at 60-80. is_autoreply (36-96). looks_pricing_or_legal (104-116) forces human escalation for price/cost/quote/budget/legal/complaint words.
LLM second (SNAP/agents/inbound_agent.py:16-81): classify_intent returns INTERESTED / DEMO_REQUESTED / OBJECTION / STOP / AUTO_REPLY with confidence, suppress_immediately, escalate_to_human and suggested_reply. It fails closed to OBJECTION, confidence 0 and escalate.
Handler (SNAP/jobs/inbound_classify_handler.py:110-221):
- INTERESTED/DEMO_REQUESTED, an LLM escalate flag, or route_action=HUMAN_ESCALATION sets lead.status=HOT_LEAD and logs an agent_event 'ESCALATE' (185-199).
- It then optionally sends a QC-reviewed 'holding' reply (_send_escalation_reply, 75-107), only if ACKNOWLEDGMENT_REPLY_ENABLED. After 2 failed QC redrafts it sends a fixed fallback text.
- Low-risk, high-confidence OBJECTION is auto-answered only if AUTO_REPLY_ENABLED, and only if QC approves (204-220).
- Replies are free-form (send_free_form_message) and logged as OutreachLog.
