Switches live in system_settings (SNAP/services/system_settings.py:12-25), default false, re-read every tick or call: discovery_enabled, autonomous_outreach_enabled, auto_reply_enabled, acknowledgment_reply_enabled. Thresholds are in config.py:112-119 (<0.70 human, 0.70-0.85 QC, >=0.85 execute, pricing always human).

findings.topic: 1f. Outbound sending, suppression, caps, watchdog
findings.detail:
Autonomous path: discovery_scheduler.run_forever (SNAP/jobs/discovery_scheduler.py:633-686) -> _run_outreach_tick (274-338) -> services/lead_service.claim_lead_for_outreach (34-145) -> jobs OUTREACH_WA (SNAP/jobs/outreach_wa_handler.py:42-200).
Controls found:
- (a) autonomous_outreach_enabled must be true (284-285, 348-349).
- (b) Daily caps default 40 per channel (config.py:76-77). They are counted as JOBS CREATED today by UTC date (_queued_today, 267-271), so the day boundary is 05:30 IST, and they count enqueued, not delivered.
- (c) 90 s stagger via run_after (329).
- (d) Region policy: channel_policies, EMAIL-only unless the country is configured (services/channel_policy_service.py:22-38).
- (e) Campaign-scoped leads need campaigns.whatsapp_outreach_approved_at (lead_service.py:107-114, re-checked in outreach_wa_handler.py:71-76 and 152-157).
- (f) is_suppressed checked before AND immediately before the send (61-65, 146-150).
- (g) Only HOT/WARM tiers with confidence >=0.70 (lead_service.py:121-126).
- (h) Watchdog: 3 consecutive bounces/failures set campaigns.watchdog_alert and pause that campaign (scheduler 318-327).
- (i) Atomic claim: UPDATE ... WHERE status='SCORED' (lead_service.py:128-133).
Follow-ups: outreach_sequences + _run_followup_tick (341-379). A WhatsApp follow-up sends only if an approved template exists for that exact level, otherwise it skips (outreach_wa_handler.py:98-110).
Suppression is normalised per channel (SNAP/services/outreach/suppression.py:21-77) and add_suppression is idempotent via the UNIQUE constraint.
A 'No' on an interest link stops the sequence but deliberately does NOT suppress (services/outreach/interest_service.py:169-180).

findings.topic: 1g. WhatsApp template machinery (what it can and cannot do)
findings.detail:
SNAP/services/outreach/whatsapp_template_service.py:
- Flow is AI/admin DRAFT -> human approve -> _create_on_meta (65-118) -> PENDING -> poll_all_pending (361, scheduler tick every 300 s) -> APPROVED/REJECTED.
- A rejection auto-drafts a replacement DRAFT (293-325), which still needs a human approve.
- Selection is product-scoped, never per-lead (get_approved_first_touch_template 408-443). Fallback is the hard-coded TEMPLATE_LIBRARY (services/outreach/whatsapp_templates.py:20-66).
- _find_by_name works around the BSP ignoring ?name= (35-46).
_create_on_meta can only build BODY (+ example) and up to 2 STATIC URL buttons (99-104). It cannot build a VIDEO/IMAGE header, FOOTER, QUICK_REPLY buttons or dynamic {{1}} URL-button suffixes.
SENDER (SNAP/services/outreach/whatsapp_service.py:34-88) supports only an IMAGE header link plus body text params. It has no video header, no 'button' component (URL suffix param), no quick-reply payloads, no media-id option.
Consequence: the approved template iv_builder_sample_video_v1 (VIDEO header + {{1}},{{2}} body + footer + URL button 'campaign/{{1}}' + 2 quick replies, see SP/wa_tpl_submit.py:103-117) can ONLY be sent by the ad-hoc scripts, never by the CRM.
That template's body is real-estate-specific ('enquiries for {{2}} arrive on WhatsApp'), so each new vertical needs a new Meta approval.

findings.topic: 1h. Human handoff, approvals and per-lead timeline that already exist
findings.detail:
APPROVALS: todo_items is a working approve/dismiss/feedback inbox (SNAP/api/todos.py:18-100; execution in SNAP/services/campaign_service.py approve_todo_item at 2138, revise_todo_item 1958, dismiss 2303). Proposal kinds already send real messages: outreach_email_draft, low-confidence batch outreach, interest-reply draft (send_interest_reply, 862+).
HANDOFF ALERTS: only a Yes-click on an email interest link calls _send_admin_alert (SNAP/services/outreach/interest_service.py:75-120): internal email plus a free-form WhatsApp to the EOD recipient numbers, then _draft_reply_for_review creates a todo. A text reply classified INTERESTED only sets HOT_LEAD and shows in the dashboard needs_response panel (api/alerts.py:42-128). It sends NO push alert to the owner. SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is declared (config.py:66) and never used.
TIMELINE: GET /leads/<id>/timeline (api/leads.py:597-684) already merges agent_events, outreach_logs and inbound_conversations chronologically.
WON: status CONVERTED exists (leads.py:34-37) but PATCH /leads/<id>/status (1011-1025) is a bare setter with no hook, no alert and no client_lifecycle row.
SAFETY NETS: stuck-lead/job/dead-job/process-down email alerts (discovery_scheduler.py:395-462) with heartbeats (services/heartbeat.py); EOD report at 23:50 IST.

findings.topic: 2. GAPS for an agent control plane (what to add)
findings.detail:
G1 Inbound buttons dropped (HIGH). SNAP/api/inbound.py:123-125 discards every non-text message. Meta docs confirm a quick-reply tap arrives as type='button' with button.payload, button.text and context.id = the wamid of the template message (source below). Voice notes, images, documents, locations and reactions are also silently dropped. Indian SMEs often reply with voice notes. Also type 'interactive' (button_reply/list_reply) is not handled.
G2 Unknown senders dropped (HIGH). inbound_service.py:60-63. Any lead messaged by the ad-hoc scripts (no CRM lead, no OutreachLog) has its reply discarded. Also create_lead (api/leads.py:739-789) stores phone strings raw while matching is exact equality on 10-digit values, so a lead created as '+91 98xxx xxxxx' would never match.
G3 No agent identity or scoped auth (HIGH). Single shared admin login (api/auth.py:16-35). An agent using it can PATCH /settings (turn autonomous outreach on), PATCH /env-settings (overwrite WHATSAPP_TOKEN etc. in .env), approve any todo (including 'Ready to send' which sets autonomous_outreach_enabled=True at campaign_service.py:2235-2243, and 'Discovery off' 2226-2233), force outreach, set any lead status. Needs per-role API keys: agent (read, create leads, propose) vs human (approve, settings).
G4 No agent_tasks / agent_runs / tool-call ledger. agent_events lacks run_id, tool name, input/output hashes, cost, actor and idempotency key. jobs has a fixed job_type set and no per-task budget.
G5 No spend ledger or caps for Apify, kie.ai, ElevenLabs or LLM. Only prospect_searches has a monthly budget (Serper X-ray only, default 0 = blocked). kie_lib.py CAP is a local file ledger with a post-hoc check.
G6 No true kill switch at the send layer. The system_settings switches are checked only in scheduler ticks and the auto-reply paths. They do NOT guard POST /leads/<id>/outreach (api/leads.py:793-900), approve_todo_item sends, send_interest_reply, send_test_outreach_preview, or whatsapp_service.send_template_message / send_free_form_message themselves (whatsapp_service.py:34, 91).
G7 No outbound rate limit beyond daily job counts (UTC day, counted at enqueue). No per-recipient lifetime cap, no per-template quality/limit awareness, no Meta tier tracking, and manual or reply sends are not counted.
G8 No push human-handoff. See 1h: text-reply INTERESTED has no notification, and CONVERTED has no hook. Admin alerts use FREE-FORM WhatsApp to the owner's number, which Meta only allows inside the 24 h customer-service window (docs below). Failures are swallowed in a try/except that only logs (interest_service.py:112-120), so a missed alert is silent. An approved UTILITY template to the owner, or Slack/email push, is needed.
G9 Per-lead asset registry is missing: page slug, video URL, template used, personalised variables, QA status, deploy and rollback state. Lead model has no consent or opt-in evidence field, which matters for Meta marketing templates.
G10 Page tracking: no view/click events from landing pages are fed back to the CRM. Only Resend opens and WhatsApp read receipts are tracked.
G11 Lead import and dedupe: the only dedupe is exact (product_id, company_name) in discovery (scraper_worker/async_runner.py:131-135). POST /leads has none. No domain, phone or RERA-id dedupe, and no way to carry source evidence (RERA id, ads URL, dossier).
G12 Interest-link flow is email-only (HMAC URLs). The WhatsApp equivalent has to reuse record_interest_response() (interest_service.py:24-49) by resolving context.id -> OutreachLog.provider_message_id -> lead.

findings.topic: 3a. Scripts reusable as agent TOOLS: WhatsApp template submit / status / send
findings.detail:
All in SP/ and designed to be piped over SSH as root. Each reads the production .env on the server, so the agent would hold root SSH plus all CRM secrets.
- wa_tpl_submit.py (video upload -> template create) is the most reusable. It already does a duplicate-name check, never deletes, scrubs secrets, and uses the verified flow GET /app -> POST /{app}/uploads -> Bearer upload -> handle -> POST /{waba}/message_templates (lines 78-120). Needs: parameterise NAME, body text, header video and buttons from a JSON spec (currently hard-coded to iv_builder_sample_video_v1, 9-12, 103-117). Add a template-spec validator (variables, footer, example values). Add a DB insert into whatsapp_templates (status PENDING + meta_template_id) so the CRM knows it. Gate behind a human approval (todo_items kind). Add idempotency via spec hash -> name. Preferably move the logic into whatsapp_template_service._create_on_meta instead of a script.
- wa_status.py is read-only GET paging of templates, hard-wired to 2 names (36). Convert to 'get template status by name' (client-side name filter, because the BSP ignores ?name=) that updates whatsapp_templates. The CRM already has poll_all_pending doing this for rows it knows.
- wa_send_test.py: a hard-coded 2-recipient allow-list assertion (14). Useful as the 'test-send-to-owner' tool pattern.
- wa_send_lead.py is the send tool prototype. It reads the recipient from a CSV, masks the number, checks the suppression list read-only against the DB across number formats, HEAD-checks the video link, and sends the template with video header + body params + URL-button suffix. Needs: remove the hard assert PROJECT_ID == '32450' (8) and the CSV, take lead_id from the CRM; go through the CRM so an OutreachLog row (with wamid) and a lead exist; enforce opt-in or first-touch policy, daily and per-lead caps, a global kill-switch check and an approval token check; idempotency key per (lead, template, day); record a send in agent_events. Today it writes nothing to the DB, so replies are unmatched (G2).
sales1.sh / sales2.sh / wa_*.sh wrappers: the mktemp-to-server + stdin-script pattern is a good secret-hygiene pattern, but it depends on a root SSH key in SP/sshkey/ that the memory notes say must be removed.

findings.topic: 3b. Scripts reusable as agent TOOLS: page deploy, video render, discovery/enrich
findings.detail:
PAGE DEPLOY (SP/deploy_campaign.sh + deploy_campaign_server.sh): has a sha256 package check, temp-copy py_compile + Jinja compile before touching live, graceful gunicorn HUP, health checks (including 404 for unknown slugs, noindex header, asset ranges), and auto-rollback by removing the route block and template (rollback(), 23-37, 114). Weaknesses to fix:
(1) Hard-wired to slug rh-7k3q9x and riverview_heights.html.
(2) It EDITS production app.py with a CAMPAIGN_PAGES dict (44-58, 92) for each new lead, which is the riskiest way to scale.
(3) 'backup skip' was chosen (20), so rollback only works in-flight and not after the fact.
(4) The site's git tree has uncommitted team edits.
(5) Runs as root over SSH.
(6) Its false-positive log check was already fixed once (SIGTERM on HUP).
Target design: a generic /campaign/<slug> route that reads data files or a DB table, so deploying a lead page = writing assets + one data row with no code edit and no HUP. Keep slug whitelist, noindex, health check, plus a 'delete slug' rollback and a per-slug versioned backup.
PAGE BUILD (SP/lead_assets/campaign_build.py, build_site.py, patch_v2/v3/v4.py): NOT reusable yet. The page text (the EN dict, campaign_build.py:17-80+) names Riverview Heights and Shree Infra in code, and build_site.py:11 hard-codes SLUG. The page was refined with string-patch scripts. Needs: a template + lead-JSON schema (SP/lead_assets/leads/shree_infra.json is the only dossier with chips, i18n and video blocks), a claims-checker and a QA step before deploy.
VIDEO: Hindi storybook pipeline = slice_voice_hi.py -> kie_stills.py/kie_videos.py (kie.ai, 8 hard-coded scene prompts and a MOTION dict) -> story_anim3.py (Playwright HTML overlays + ffmpeg). It is Windows-bound (ffmpeg-win-x86_64-v7.1.exe path at story_anim3.py:17, local Playwright venv), scenes and strings are Riverview-specific (story_anim3.py:287,335,358), the voice is a hand-recorded ElevenLabs MP3 (free plan blocks library voices over the API), and captions are estimated because no ASR works for Gujarati/Hinglish. Treat as a reference implementation, not a tool. A per-lead video tool would need a scene-script input, a TTS provider API with a paid plan, a Linux ffmpeg/Playwright image, an output size/length cap (WhatsApp video limit not verified here), and a human preview gate.
SPEND CAP (kie_lib.py): useful pattern with a CAP=300 constant (11), a ledger file, create() calls guard() first. But the check is post-hoc (it uses the last recorded balance, so a batch can overshoot before the ledger updates), it is a local un-locked JSON file (race with parallel agents), a single global cap with no per-lead or per-day dimension, and the key is a plaintext file at a Windows home path.
DISCOVERY/ENRICH: RERA/Maps/Ads discovery was done by Claude calling the Apify MCP connector and curl against GujRERA's undocumented API. No script exists, and the 'pay score' and 'audit' helpers (SP/cands.py, SP/round3/analyze.py) are one-off. The CRM has its own Serper/Maps/Hunter DISCOVER/ENRICH/REVIEW/SCORE pipeline (SNAP/scraper_worker/async_runner.py:79-512), but it knows nothing of Apify, RERA or Meta Ads. Lead CSVs (round3/*.csv, round4/trigger_leads_2026-10-14.csv with 30 rows, 25 columns) are flat plaintext PII and do not match the CRM lead schema.

findings.topic: 4. Safest minimal FIRST integration point
findings.detail:
Make the INBOUND side complete first. It sends nothing, it is mandatory before any pilot (otherwise replies vanish), and it can be tested end-to-end with the owner's own two numbers that already received the template.
In SNAP/api/inbound.py (_handle_one_message, 121-139):
(1) Accept type 'button' and 'interactive' and store media types as text placeholders such as '[voice note]' with the raw payload.
(2) Resolve button/interactive replies deterministically. Use context.id to find OutreachLog.provider_message_id -> lead. Map payload 'Yes, send the sample' to record_interest_response(db, lead, log, 'YES') (reuses idempotency, HOT_LEAD, sequence stop, admin alert, reply-draft todo). Map 'No, thanks' to the NO path, which stops the sequence without suppression.
(3) Keep the existing STOP handling for typed text.
(4) Add an unmatched-sender inbox row (nullable lead_id or an 'orphan_inbound' table) instead of dropping.
(5) Verify the webhook signature if the BSP signs.
Then, as the second step, add a read-only 'agent' blueprint under /api/v1/agent/ with its own bearer key. It exposes lead get/list, timeline, templates, and settings state, plus append-only POST /agent/events and POST /agent/proposals (writes todo_items with new proposal kinds). No send, status, settings or approve routes. The agent then does research, dossier, pitch decision and drafting while every side effect goes through the existing human-approval todo flow.
Only after both are stable: harden send_template_message (add video header, button components, global kill-switch check, idempotency key) and let an approved 'agent_wa_send' proposal call it for ONE pilot lead via a campaign whose whatsapp_outreach_approved_at is still NULL until the human approves.
The pilot lead must exist in the CRM first: create it through POST /leads with a normalized 10-digit phone, so inbound matching works.

findings.topic: 5a. Risks: security
findings.detail:
S1 Unsigned, guessable inbound webhook (HIGH). POST /api/v1/inbound/whatsapp (SNAP/api/inbound.py:38) checks nothing: the verify token only guards the GET handshake (28-35). Anyone who can reach the URL can forge messages from any lead's number. A forged 'STOP' permanently suppresses that lead (inbound_service.py:66-69); a forged INTERESTED triggers HOT_LEAD, LLM spend and possibly a free-form acknowledgement. The comment in webhooks.py:14-17 assumes a 'random' URL, but the route is the predictable /api/v1/inbound/whatsapp. Meta's documented method is HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the app secret in X-Hub-Signature-256 (source below). Whether this BSP signs with a secret the CRM can access is UNVERIFIED.
S2 Outreach-approval link is a GET, unauthenticated, non-expiring, non-single-use HMAC URL (SNAP/api/outreach_approval.py:20-39; services/outreach/outreach_approval_links.py:19-38). The test-preview email contains the EMAIL and WHATSAPP approve links together, and email scanners or link prefetchers commonly open links automatically (the codebase itself notes this for Yes/No links: models.py:549-557 comment, interest_service). A prefetch would unlock real WhatsApp sends to a whole campaign with no human decision. Treat the 'campaign approval' gate as weaker than it looks until it uses POST + confirm, or a short expiry.
S3 Shared single admin credential, no rate limit on /auth/login (public), no roles. The same session can write secrets into .env (api/env_settings.py:18-38). See G3.
S4 Approving certain todos has global side effects (campaign_service.py:2226-2243). If an agent shares the human's session it can self-approve. Approval endpoints must be human-only.
S5 PII in logs: phone numbers logged at info level (whatsapp_service.py:87,120; inbound_service.py:62,69,98; outreach_wa_handler.py:199). Defaults for the owner's email and phone are hard-coded in config.py:82-85 and system_settings.py:184-185.
S6 Prompt injection surface: the lead's message text is embedded in the LLM prompt (agents/inbound_agent.py:35-41). Outputs are enum/clamped and QC-reviewed, but suggested_reply is sent to the lead on escalation (inbound_classify_handler.py:75-107). Keep the QC gate. Never let the classifier output drive tool calls.
S7 All CRM processes run as root; an SSH root key from this session is still in SP/sshkey and must be revoked (per memory notes); the ElevenLabs and Apify keys pasted in chat earlier are still unrevoked per memory.
S8 The snapshot at SP/sales_snap/code/backend contains sales_system.db-wal (5.5 MB) and -shm (also inside code.tgz): live CRM data including lead PII sitting in a temp scratchpad. Delete when no longer needed.

findings.topic: 5b. Risks: sending, data and reliability
findings.detail:
R1 STOP over-matching (MEDIUM). hard_classifiers.py:19 \bstop\b matches any message containing 'stop' ('don't stop', 'bus stop') and the opt-out list includes 'not interested' (21) and 'no thanks' (28). Result is permanent suppression with no human review (inbound_service.py:66-69). This is conservative for compliance but loses real leads. Note the template button text 'No, thanks' has a comma and does NOT match '\bno thanks?\b', so a mis-routed button reply would not be suppressed by the regex.
R2 Manual trigger resets status (MEDIUM). POST /leads/<id>/outreach sets any non-SCORED lead back to SCORED (api/leads.py:835-836) including HOT_LEAD, CONVERTED and REJECTED, then sends. Suppression and campaign approval still apply, but a WON client can be re-pitched. Agent keys must not reach this route.
R3 Duplicate / over-cap exposure (MEDIUM). Caps count enqueued jobs by UTC day, ignore manual, reply and ad-hoc sends, and there is no per-recipient lifetime cap. Ad-hoc script sends bypass all of it, including OutreachLog, suppression writes and the watchdog.
R4 Free-form replies assume an open 24 h window 'by construction' (whatsapp_service.py:91-100), but classify jobs can run late (queue backlog, retries); a late reply then fails and is just retried. Admin alerts fail silently outside the window.
R5 SQLite with 7+ writer processes. Already caused a 16 h scheduler outage (models.py:333-362 comment) and 'database is locked' worker crashes (jobs/worker.py:39-53). An always-on multi-agent writer adds contention; keep agent writes short and batched, or plan Postgres.
R6 Stuck-claim handling is detect-and-alert only (discovery_scheduler.py:397-399). A crashed worker leaves jobs CLAIMED forever, so agent tasks need lease timeouts.
R7 Dedupe is weak (G11): the same business can be created twice and messaged twice from different sources.
R8 Compliance coupling: Meta marketing templates need opt-in; the pitch to RERA promoters touches RERA Act s.3 advertising limits; the Shree Infra <-> ads link was never verified (memory note). A cold WhatsApp template to scraped numbers is a quality-rating and account-ban risk for the only WABA the company has.
R9 Test-preview default recipient and EOD recipients point at the owner's real number; a bug in preview or tests could message the wrong target if settings are wiped (system_settings.py:184-185).
R10 Template names and meta_template_id live in two places (DB row vs scripts). A script-created template (iv_builder_sample_video_v1) has no whatsapp_templates row, so the CRM cannot select it.

recommendations: Do not give the agent the shared admin session. First add a separate agent bearer-key auth (a before_request branch) restricted to an allow-list of routes, and make approve/settings/env-settings/status/force-outreach human-session-only. Without this every other control can be self-bypassed.

Complete inbound first (SNAP/api/inbound.py:121-139): accept button/interactive/media types, resolve context.id to OutreachLog.provider_message_id -> lead, map 'Yes, send the sample' to record_interest_response(YES) and 'No, thanks' to the NO path, and store unmatched senders instead of dropping. Test with the owner's two numbers that already hold the template message.

Add a webhook signature check (X-Hub-Signature-256, HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the app secret, per Meta docs) if the BSP provides an app secret. Otherwise add a secret path token, an IP allow-list at LiteSpeed, and a rate limit.

Add agent control-plane tables via schema.sql: agent_tasks (type, lead_id, state, lease_until, idempotency_key, budget), agent_runs, agent_tool_calls (tool, args hash, result ref, cost, run_id), agent_approvals (or reuse todo_items with new proposal kinds), spend_ledger (provider, amount, day, lead_id, cap), lead_assets (slug, page/video/template refs, QA status, deploy version), lead_enrichment (source evidence JSON, consent/opt-in, dedupe keys). Reuse agent_events as the human-readable audit feed by adding run_id.

Put a real kill switch in the send layer: check a global_send_enabled setting plus a per-channel switch inside whatsapp_service.send_template_message and send_free_form_message (and the email service), so no route, script or approval can send while it is off. Surface it as one big button in the dashboard and a WhatsApp command to the owner.

Extend send_template_message with header video link (or media id), a 'button' component for URL suffix, and quick-reply payloads, and create the whatsapp_templates row for iv_builder_sample_video_v1 so the CRM can select and track it. Route every send through the CRM so OutreachLog (with wamid), suppression and caps always apply. Retire wa_send_lead.py as a production path.

Replace per-lead app.py edits for landing pages with a data-driven generic /campaign/<slug> route (slug whitelist from a table or JSON directory, noindex, no HUP needed) and a slug-level versioned backup plus delete-slug rollback. Add page-view logging that writes to the CRM so replies and views correlate.

Wrap each external tool (Apify run, kie.ai, ElevenLabs, LLM) in a spend-capped function: pre-estimate cost, reserve against a daily and per-lead cap in the ledger under a DB lock, fail closed, record actuals. Keep the kie_lib ledger idea but make it a shared, locked table, not a local file.

Use a human-handoff channel that is not limited by the 24 h window: an approved UTILITY template to the owner plus email/Slack push (SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is already declared). Trigger it from CONVERTED and INTERESTED events, not only the email Yes-click. Fill client_lifecycle on CONVERTED.

Give the agent a Linux worker, not the Windows desktop: move ffmpeg/Playwright/video tooling and keys to the VPS (or a separate box) running as a non-root user, with a secrets file readable only by that user. Revoke the leaked ElevenLabs/Apify keys and the root SSH key from the scratchpad before any 24/7 run.

Before enabling WhatsApp pilots, resolve the opt-in/quality question: marketing templates to scraped numbers risk the only WABA. Start with owner-numbers and a handful of explicitly human-approved first touches; keep AUTO_REPLY and ACK switches off until button handling is verified.
Delete sales_system.db-wal/-shm and code.tgz from the scratchpad once the snapshot is no longer needed.
risks: HIGH: the unsigned, predictable inbound webhook (SNAP/api/inbound.py:38) lets anyone forge STOP or INTERESTED for any lead number. STOP means permanent suppression, INTERESTED means HOT_LEAD, LLM spend and possible replies.

HIGH: shared admin session means an agent using it could turn on autonomous outreach, rewrite WHATSAPP_TOKEN in .env, or approve its own proposals (campaign_service.py:2226-2243). There is no scoped credential.

HIGH: the campaign send-approval gate is a plain unauthenticated GET HMAC link that never expires (api/outreach_approval.py:20-39). A mail-scanner prefetch of the test-preview email could unlock real WhatsApp and email outreach for a whole campaign.

HIGH: replies to any message sent outside the CRM (all ad-hoc script sends) are dropped (inbound_service.py:60-63) and button taps / voice notes are dropped for all senders (inbound.py:123-125). A pilot would look like silence even when leads answered.
MEDIUM: kill switch exists only in scheduler ticks. Manual route, approvals and the send functions themselves can still send when 'off'.
MEDIUM: production processes run as root with the SSH key and API keys from this session still outstanding; a prod DB WAL with PII sits in the scratchpad.
MEDIUM: SQLite plus seven writer processes has caused a 16 h scheduler stall and worker crashes; a 24/7 multi-agent writer raises this risk.
MEDIUM: Meta account and quality risk from cold marketing templates to scraped numbers; RERA advertising rules; unverified ad-owner links (Shree Infra vs 'Patel Group' branding).
LOW/MED: STOP regex over-matches; admin alerts depend on the 24 h free-form window and fail silently; caps use UTC day and count enqueued jobs.
open_questions: Does waba.fortius.in.net sign its webhook calls (X-Hub-Signature-256) and with what secret, or does it relay them unsigned? Unverified; BSP docs not checked.

What is the BSP's actual inbound 'button' payload shape? Meta's reference shows type='button' with button.payload/text and context.id (verified), but the Fortius relay may reshape it. Capture one real tap payload (from the owner's test message) before coding.
Is the webhook currently registered at the BSP pointing at /api/v1/inbound/whatsapp? The snapshot cannot show it.
Which of the 4 system_settings switches and the campaign approval timestamps are ON in production right now? The DB itself was not in the snapshot.
Has wa_send_lead.py ever been run against the real Shree Infra number? Memory notes say only owner-number test sends happened; the script contains a real-recipient path.
Systemd/cron for the CRM: memory says bos-* units, the 2026-10-09 snapshot found none; how are the 5 processes supervised (screen? manual?) and do they survive a reboot?
Does the company have a Meta app secret, a Meta Business verification, and messaging-limit tier visible, so quality-rating throttling can be designed?

WhatsApp video size/duration limit for template header sends was not verified here (Meta page I fetched gave no limits), and neither was the Meta doc's video-header send JSON; the working structure is only evidenced by the ad-hoc scripts' accepted test sends.
How should a human say 'won'? A dashboard click (PATCH status CONVERTED), a WhatsApp command, or an agent-detected event confirmed by the human? This decides where the handoff hook lives.
